由[歐仁·德拉克羅瓦](/wiki/%E6%AC%A7%E4%BB%81%C2%B7%E5%BE%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E7%BD%97%E7%93%A6 "欧仁·德拉克罗瓦")所繪的《[阿爾及爾的女人](/w/index.php?title=%E9%98%BF%E7%88%BE%E5%8F%8A%E7%88%BE%E7%9A%84%E5%A5%B3%E4%BA%BA&action=edit&redlink=1 "阿爾及爾的女人（页面不存在）")（英语：[Women of Algiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_of_Algiers "en:Women of Algiers")）》(1834年)，收藏於[巴黎](/wiki/%E5%B7%B4%E9%BB%8E "巴黎")[羅浮宮](/wiki/%E7%BE%85%E6%B5%AE%E5%AE%AE "羅浮宮")。

東方主義是指東方文化，這是相對於，並對立於[西方文化](/wiki/%E8%A5%BF%E6%B4%8B "西洋")的概念。兩者分別代表東方與西方。[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)"Orient"這個字經由中古法語的"orient"進入英語。其字根"oriēns"來自拉丁語的"Oriēns"，具有多個同義指涉：世界的東方部分、太陽升起的星空、東方、上升的太陽等。然而，其指涉隨著在地理上使用而產生變化。

有英詩之父的[傑弗瑞·喬叟](/wiki/%E6%9D%B0%E5%BC%97%E9%87%8C%C2%B7%E4%B9%94%E5%8F%9F "杰弗里·乔叟")在他撰寫的[僧侶的故事](/w/index.php?title=%E5%83%A7%E4%BE%B6%E7%9A%84%E6%95%85%E4%BA%8B&action=edit&redlink=1 "僧侶的故事（页面不存在）")（英语：[The Monk's Tale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monk%27s_Tale "en:The Monk's Tale")）（1375年）中，寫道：'That they conquered many regnes grete / In the orient, with many a fair citee.'（他們在東方征服許多偉大的王國與許多美麗的城市）。在此，"orient"是指[地中海](/wiki/%E5%9C%B0%E4%B8%AD%E6%B5%B7 "地中海")和[南歐](/wiki/%E5%8D%97%E6%AD%90 "南歐")以東的地區。[英國工黨](/wiki/%E5%B7%A5%E9%BB%A8_(%E8%8B%B1%E5%9C%8B) "工黨 (英國)")政治人物[安奈林·貝文](/wiki/%E5%AE%89%E5%A5%88%E6%9E%97%C2%B7%E8%B2%9D%E6%96%87 "安奈林·貝文")在他撰寫的《[恐懼之位](/w/index.php?title=%E6%81%90%E6%87%BC%E4%B9%8B%E4%BD%8D&action=edit&redlink=1 "恐懼之位（页面不存在）")（英语：[In Place of Fear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_Place_of_Fear "en:In Place of Fear")）》（1952年）中，在'在西方思想衝擊下覺醒的東方'的描述中，將東方定義擴展，納入[東亞](/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%9E "東亞")。愛德華·薩依德表示，'東方主義是一種工具，讓西方得以在政治、經濟、文化與社會各個領域來統治東方。這種影響力不僅存在於過去的殖民時代，也延續到現在。'[[7]](#cite_note-7)

### 藝術

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=3 "编辑章节：藝術")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Anonymous_Venetian_orientalist_painting%2C_The_Reception_of_the_Ambassadors_in_Damascus%27%2C_1511%2C_the_Louvre.jpg/330px-Anonymous_Venetian_orientalist_painting%2C_The_Reception_of_the_Ambassadors_in_Damascus%27%2C_1511%2C_the_Louvre.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](/wiki/File:Anonymous_Venetian_orientalist_painting,_The_Reception_of_the_Ambassadors_in_Damascus%27,_1511,_the_Louvre.jpg)

[威尼斯](/wiki/%E5%A8%81%E5%B0%BC%E6%96%AF "威尼斯")無名畫家所繪《在[大馬士革](/wiki/%E5%A4%A7%E9%A6%AC%E5%A3%AB%E9%9D%A9 "大馬士革")接見使節》（The Reception of the Ambassadors in Damascus）（1511年），收藏於[羅浮宮](/wiki/%E7%BE%85%E6%B5%AE%E5%AE%AE "羅浮宮")。據悉前景中長角的鹿從未在[敘利亞](/wiki/%E6%95%98%E5%88%A9%E4%BA%9E "敘利亞")的野外出現過。

在藝術史中，東方主義指的是主要活躍於19世紀的西方藝術家作品，他們專門研究東方題材，並根據19世紀在西亞的旅遊經歷來創作。當時從事相關創作與研究的藝術家和學者被統稱為"東方主義者"。特別是在[法國](/wiki/%E6%B3%95%E5%9C%8B "法國")，藝術評論家[朱爾斯·安托萬·卡斯塔尼亞里](/w/index.php?title=%E6%9C%B1%E7%88%BE%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E5%AE%89%E6%89%98%E8%90%AC%C2%B7%E5%8D%A1%E6%96%AF%E5%A1%94%E5%B0%BC%E4%BA%9E%E9%87%8C&action=edit&redlink=1 "朱爾斯·安托萬·卡斯塔尼亞里（页面不存在）")（英语：[Jules-Antoine Castagnary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules-Antoine_Castagnary "en:Jules-Antoine Castagnary")）的推波助瀾，使得這個用語開始帶有貶義色彩，並在社會上廣泛流傳。[[8]](#cite_note-8)雖然社會對這種具象藝術風格存在蔑視，[法蘭西東方畫家協會](/w/index.php?title=%E6%B3%95%E8%98%AD%E8%A5%BF%E6%9D%B1%E6%96%B9%E7%95%AB%E5%AE%B6%E5%8D%94%E6%9C%83&action=edit&redlink=1 "法蘭西東方畫家協會（页面不存在）")（英语：[Sociétédes Peintres OrientalistesFrançais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9des_Peintres_OrientalistesFran%C3%A7ais "en:Sociétédes Peintres OrientalistesFrançais")）仍於1893年成立，並由[尚-李奧·傑洛姆](/wiki/%E5%B0%9A-%E6%9D%8E%E5%A5%A7%C2%B7%E5%82%91%E6%B4%9B%E5%A7%86 "尚-李奧·傑洛姆")（當時學院派的領袖，也是反對正在崛起的印象派最力的藝術家）擔任名譽主席。[[9]](#cite_note-9)而在英國，"東方主義者"則被界定為"一種藝術家"。[[10]](#cite_note-10)

法蘭西東方畫家協會在19世紀末成立後，從業者的意識為之改變，因為藝術家們現在可將自己視為一個獨特藝術運動中的一種。.[[11]](#cite_note-11)東方主義繪畫作通常被視為19世紀學院藝術的眾多分支之一。然而各種不同風格的東方主義藝術也隨之出現。藝術史學家傾向於將東方主義藝術家區分為兩大類：一類是仔細描繪所見事物的現實主義者，如[德國](/wiki/%E5%BE%B7%E5%9C%8B "德國")畫家[古斯塔夫·鮑恩芬德](/w/index.php?title=%E5%8F%A4%E6%96%AF%E5%A1%94%E5%A4%AB%C2%B7%E9%AE%91%E6%81%A9%E8%8A%AC%E5%BE%B7&action=edit&redlink=1 "古斯塔夫·鮑恩芬德（页面不存在）")（英语：[Gustav Bauernfeind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_Bauernfeind "en:Gustav Bauernfeind")），另一類則是從未離開畫室、全憑想像建構東方場景的人。[[[12]](#cite_note-12)法國畫家如[歐仁·德拉克洛瓦](/wiki/%E6%AD%90%E4%BB%81%C2%B7%E5%BE%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E6%B4%9B%E7%93%A6 "歐仁·德拉克洛瓦")（生卒年份1798–1863年）和尚-李奧·傑洛姆（生卒年份1824–1904年）兩位，被廣泛視為東方主義運動的領軍人物。[[13]](#cite_note-13)

### 東方研究

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=4 "编辑章节：東方研究")]

主条目：[東方研究](/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E6%96%B9%E7%A0%94%E7%A9%B6 "東方研究")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Georg_August_Wallin_by_Robert_Wilhelm_Ekman_-_Arppeanum_-_DSC05234.JPG/250px-Georg_August_Wallin_by_Robert_Wilhelm_Ekman_-_Arppeanum_-_DSC05234.JPG?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](/wiki/File:Georg_August_Wallin_by_Robert_Wilhelm_Ekman_-_Arppeanum_-_DSC05234.JPG)

[芬蘭](/wiki/%E8%8A%AC%E8%98%AD "芬蘭")[G·A·瓦林](/w/index.php?title=G%C2%B7A%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E6%9E%97&action=edit&redlink=1 "G·A·瓦林（页面不存在）")（英语：[Georg August Wallin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_August_Wallin "en:Georg August Wallin")）教授（生卒年份1811–1852年）是一位探險家與東方學家，他因在1840年代加入首批在中東地區學習與旅行的歐洲人而聞名。[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15)[[16]](#cite_note-16)此肖像由[R·W·埃克曼](/w/index.php?title=R%C2%B7W%C2%B7%E5%9F%83%E5%85%8B%E6%9B%BC&action=edit&redlink=1 "R·W·埃克曼（页面不存在）")（英语：[Robert Wilhelm Ekman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wilhelm_Ekman "en:Robert Wilhelm Ekman")）繪於1853年。

東方主義者在18世紀末、19世紀和20世紀初，"是指專門研究東方世界語言和文學的學者。這些學者中，有些是[英國東印度公司](/wiki/%E8%8B%B1%E5%9C%8B%E6%9D%B1%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E5%85%AC%E5%8F%B8 "英國東印度公司")的官員，他們主張[阿拉伯文化](/wiki/%E9%98%BF%E6%8B%89%E4%BC%AF%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96 "阿拉伯文化")、[印度文化](/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96 "印度文化")和[伊斯蘭文化](/wiki/%E4%BC%8A%E6%96%AF%E8%98%AD%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96 "伊斯蘭文化")應被視為與歐洲文化平等的對象來進行研究。[[17]](#cite_note-17)這些學者中包括[語文學](/wiki/%E8%AA%9E%E6%96%87%E5%AD%B8 "語文學")家[威廉·瓊斯](/wiki/%E5%A8%81%E5%BB%89%C2%B7%E7%90%BC%E6%96%AF_(%E8%AF%AD%E8%A8%80%E5%AD%A6%E5%AE%B6) "威廉·琼斯 (语言学家)")，他對[印歐語系](/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E6%AD%90%E8%AA%9E%E7%B3%BB "印歐語系")的研究得以建立起現代語文學。東印度公司在統治[印度次大陸](/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E6%AC%A1%E5%A4%A7%E9%99%B8 "印度次大陸")期間曾支持東方主義，將其作為發展，並維持與當地人良好關係的手段 - 直到1820年代，受[麥考利男爵](/wiki/%E7%AC%AC%E4%B8%80%E4%BB%A3%E9%BA%A6%E8%80%83%E5%88%A9%E7%94%B7%E7%88%B5%E6%89%98%E9%A9%AC%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E5%AE%BE%E9%A1%BF%C2%B7%E9%BA%A6%E8%80%83%E5%88%A9 "第一代麦考利男爵托马斯·巴宾顿·麦考利")和[約翰·史都華·彌爾](/wiki/%E7%B4%84%E7%BF%B0%C2%B7%E5%8F%B2%E9%83%BD%E8%8F%AF%C2%B7%E5%BD%8C%E7%88%BE "約翰·史都華·彌爾")等"英語化派"（anglicists）倡導者的影響，開始轉向推廣西式教育。[[18]](#cite_note-18)

此外，[希伯來主義](/w/index.php?title=%E5%B8%8C%E4%BC%AF%E4%BE%86%E4%B8%BB%E7%BE%A9&action=edit&redlink=1 "希伯來主義（页面不存在）")（英语：[Hebraism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebraism "en:Hebraism")）和[猶太學](/wiki/%E7%8A%B9%E5%A4%AA%E5%AD%A6 "犹太学")在19和20世紀的英、德學者中也頗受歡迎。[[19]](#cite_note-19)原本涵蓋近東與遠東文化的東方研究，在20世紀因殖民體系瓦解與學術專業化而發生轉型。學者們捨棄過去將廣大亞洲視為同質整體的模糊視角，轉而將學術領域精確拆分為：研究西亞與北非的中東研究，以及探討[南亞](/wiki/%E5%8D%97%E4%BA%9E "南亞")、[東南亞](/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E5%8D%97%E4%BA%9E "東南亞")與[東亞](/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%9E "東亞")的亞洲研究。象徵學術界試圖擺脫殖民偏見，轉向更具主體性且精確的研究路向。

### 批判性研究

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=5 "编辑章节：批判性研究")]

#### 愛德華·薩依德

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=6 "编辑章节：愛德華·薩依德")]

文化評論家愛德華·薩依德在其著作《東方學》中，重新定義東方主義這個用語，用以描述一種普遍存在的西方傳統 - 包括在學術和藝術層面 - 即對東方世界帶有偏見的外來者詮釋，這種詮釋是由18和19世紀歐洲[帝國主義](/wiki/%E5%B8%9D%E5%9C%8B%E4%B8%BB%E7%BE%A9 "帝國主義")的文化態度所塑造。[[20]](#cite_note-20) 《東方學》的論點發展出[安東尼奧·葛蘭西](/wiki/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%9C%E5%B0%BC%E5%A5%A5%C2%B7%E8%91%9B%E5%85%B0%E8%A5%BF "安东尼奥·葛兰西")的[文化霸權](/wiki/%E6%96%87%E5%8C%96%E9%9C%B8%E6%AC%8A "文化霸權")理論，以及[米歇爾·傅柯](/wiki/%E7%B1%B3%E6%AD%87%E7%88%BE%C2%B7%E5%82%85%E6%9F%AF "米歇爾·傅柯")的[話語](/wiki/%E8%A9%B1%E8%AA%9E "話語")理論（[知識](/wiki/%E7%9F%A5%E8%AD%98 "知識")與[權力](/wiki/%E6%AC%8A%E5%8A%9B "權力")的關係），以此來批判東方研究的學術傳統。薩依德批評當代那些延續對阿拉伯-伊斯蘭文化外來者詮釋傳統的學者，特別是[伯納德·劉易斯](/wiki/%E4%BC%AF%E7%B4%8D%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E5%8A%89%E6%98%93%E6%96%AF "伯納德·劉易斯")（英裔美國猶太歷史學者）和[福阿德·阿賈米](/wiki/%E7%A6%8F%E9%98%BF%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E9%98%BF%E8%B4%BE%E7%B1%B3 "福阿德·阿贾米")（黎巴嫩裔-美國教授）[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-Xypolia2011-22)薩依德又表示：'[再現](/wiki/%E8%A1%A8%E5%BE%B5_(%E8%97%9D%E8%A1%93) "表徵 (藝術)")的概念是戲劇性的：東方是一個舞台，整個東方都被限制在上面（可概括表達為這些東方主義者的再現，並非對客觀現實的簡單反映，而是他們透過特定文化框架建構東方形象的行為。而將東方置於被動的地位，使其成為西方觀察、定義與統治的對象），[[23]](#cite_note-23)且博學的東方主義者的主題'與其說是東方本身，不如說是（加工過的）呈現給西方讀者大眾、因而不再那麼令人生畏的東方'。[[24]](#cite_note-24)

東方學作為一門學科，有悠久的歷史，但愛德華·薩依德於1978年出版的著述卻被視為後殖民研究的奠基之作。其原因在於這本書首次將東方學視為一種與殖民權力緊密結合的論述，徹底改變學界對跨文化研究中權力關係的理解。[[25]](#cite_note-25)薩依德著作中的分析主要針對歐洲文學（特別是法國文學）中的東方主義，並未分析視覺藝術和東方主義繪畫。沿著這一思路，[美國](/wiki/%E7%BE%8E%E5%9C%8B "美國")藝術史學家[琳達·諾克林](/w/index.php?title=%E7%90%B3%E9%81%94%C2%B7%E8%AB%BE%E5%85%8B%E6%9E%97&action=edit&redlink=1 "琳達·諾克林（页面不存在）")（英语：[Linda Nochlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Nochlin "en:Linda Nochlin")）將薩依德的批判分析方法應用於藝術，但"所得結果參差不齊"。[[26]](#cite_note-26)其他學者則認為東方主義繪畫所描繪的是一種神話和幻想，通常與現實不符。[[27]](#cite_note-27)

薩依德的的理論影響後來的文化評論，讓學界開始注意到：現代工業與科技如何進一步加深西方對東方的誤解。這種誤解體現在科技東方主義（Techno-Orientalism，承認東方科技先進，但認為東方人缺乏靈魂、冷酷且非人化）或後現代東方主義（postmodern Orientalism，剝離東方文化的歷史深度，僅把它當作是種消費裝飾）等現象中。[[28]](#cite_note-28)

#### 伊斯蘭世界

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=7 "编辑章节：伊斯蘭世界")]

伊斯蘭世界內部也存在一種批判東方主義的趨勢。據一項在2002年所作的估計，僅在[沙烏地阿拉伯](/wiki/%E6%B2%99%E7%83%8F%E5%9C%B0%E9%98%BF%E6%8B%89%E4%BC%AF "沙烏地阿拉伯")，當地或外國學者就撰寫約200本書籍和2,000篇討論東方主義的文章。[[29]](#cite_note-29)

**東亞的東方主義** 雖然薩依德的基礎框架主要集中在中東和阿拉伯世界，但學者們已將針對東方主義的分析擴展到東亞，特別是在[中國](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9C%8B "中國")。具體而言，早年西方的[傳教士](/wiki/%E5%82%B3%E6%95%99%E5%A3%AB "傳教士")與外交使節在與中國接觸的過程中，透過其書信、報告與條約談判，建構出一套截然不同的文化再現模式（傳教士通常從宗教與道德的角度詮釋中國的禮教社會，而外交官則多從[國際關係](/wiki/%E5%9C%8B%E9%9A%9B%E9%97%9C%E4%BF%82 "國際關係")與貿易利益出發，將中國形塑為一個停滯不前或封閉自大的古老帝國。）。[[30]](#cite_note-30)

**傳教士對中國的視角** 在[第一次鴉片戰爭](/wiki/%E7%AC%AC%E4%B8%80%E6%AC%A1%E9%B4%89%E7%89%87%E6%88%B0%E7%88%AD "第一次鴉片戰爭")（1839-1842年）期間進入中國的西方基督傳教士，在塑造西方對中國的看法方面發揮有重要作用。他們的活動在中國社會引發廣泛的懷疑和抵制。傳教士在中國的活動與報告，往往與其母國（如[大英帝國](/wiki/%E5%A4%A7%E8%8B%B1%E5%B8%9D%E5%9C%8B "大英帝國")或[法國](/wiki/%E6%B3%95%E5%9C%8B "法國")）的帝國利益緊密相關。[[31]](#cite_note-31)

**神聖東方主義** 一份相關期刊提出稱為"神聖東方主義"的概念，描述如[西班牙](/wiki/%E8%A5%BF%E7%8F%AD%E7%89%99 "西班牙")傳教士[胡安·岡薩雷斯·德·門多薩](/wiki/%E8%83%A1%E5%AE%89%C2%B7%E5%86%88%E8%90%A8%E9%9B%B7%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E9%97%A8%E5%A4%9A%E8%90%A8 "胡安·冈萨雷斯·德·门多萨")等傳教士[民族誌](/wiki/%E6%B0%91%E6%97%8F%E8%AA%8C "民族誌")學者如何將亞洲的宗教和倫理生活理想化，建構出一個令人景仰的"神聖東方"，作為對西方物質主義的一種隱含道德對比 - 這是一種更微妙但同樣具有扭曲性的東方主義再現形式。[[32]](#cite_note-32)

## 建築與設計

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=8 "编辑章节：建築與設計")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/MoscheeSchwetzingen_Panorama_quad.jpg/250px-MoscheeSchwetzingen_Panorama_quad.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](/wiki/File:MoscheeSchwetzingen_Panorama_quad.jpg)

位於德國[施韋青根](/wiki/%E6%96%BD%E9%9F%A6%E9%9D%92%E6%A0%B9 "施韦青根")，[施韋青根宮](/wiki/%E6%96%BD%E9%9F%A6%E9%9D%92%E6%A0%B9%E5%AE%AB "施韦青根宫")花園內的[巴洛克](/wiki/%E5%B7%B4%E6%B4%9B%E5%85%8B "巴洛克")式紅色[清真寺](/wiki/%E6%B8%85%E7%9C%9F%E5%AF%BA "清真寺")。這是18世紀歐洲所建的花園清真寺中唯一倖存的範例，由[尼古拉·德·皮加熱](/w/index.php?title=%E5%B0%BC%E5%8F%A4%E6%8B%89%C2%B7%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E7%9A%AE%E5%8A%A0%E7%86%B1&action=edit&redlink=1 "尼古拉·德·皮加熱（页面不存在）")（英语：[Nicolas de Pigage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_de_Pigage "en:Nicolas de Pigage")）於1779–1795年間建造。[[33]](#cite_note-33)

[文藝復興](/wiki/%E6%96%87%E8%97%9D%E5%BE%A9%E8%88%88 "文藝復興")裝飾中的[摩爾紋樣式](/w/index.php?title=%E6%91%A9%E7%88%BE%E7%B4%8B%E6%A8%A3%E5%BC%8F&action=edit&redlink=1 "摩爾紋樣式（页面不存在）")（英语：[Moresque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moresque "en:Moresque")）是歐洲對伊斯蘭式[阿拉伯紋樣](/wiki/%E9%98%BF%E6%8B%89%E4%BC%AF%E7%B4%8B%E6%A8%A3 "阿拉伯紋樣")的改編，始於15世紀末，並一直用於某些類型的作品（如書籍裝幀），直到近乎今日。早期建築中使用來自[印度次大陸](/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E6%AC%A1%E5%A4%A7%E9%99%B8 "印度次大陸")的圖案被稱為[印度撒拉遜復興建築](/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E6%92%92%E6%8B%89%E9%81%9C%E5%BE%A9%E8%88%88%E5%BB%BA%E7%AF%89 "印度撒拉遜復興建築")。最早的例子之一是[倫敦](/wiki/%E5%80%AB%E6%95%A6 "倫敦")[市政廳 (倫敦)](/wiki/%E5%B8%82%E6%94%BF%E5%BB%B3_(%E5%80%AB%E6%95%A6) "市政廳 (倫敦)")的正立面（1788-1789年）。這種風格隨著[威廉·霍奇斯](/w/index.php?title=%E5%A8%81%E5%BB%89%C2%B7%E9%9C%8D%E5%A5%87%E6%96%AF&action=edit&redlink=1 "威廉·霍奇斯（页面不存在）")（英语：[William Hodges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hodges "en:William Hodges")）、[威廉·丹尼爾](/wiki/%E5%A8%81%E5%BB%89%C2%B7%E4%B8%B9%E5%B0%BC%E5%B0%94 "威廉·丹尼尔")}與[托馬斯·丹尼爾](/wiki/%E6%89%98%E9%A9%AC%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E4%B8%B9%E5%B0%BC%E5%B0%94 "托马斯·丹尼尔")在1795年左右出版的印度景觀圖集後，在西方更為盛行。

[土耳其風](/w/index.php?title=%E5%9C%9F%E8%80%B3%E5%85%B6%E9%A2%A8&action=edit&redlink=1 "土耳其風（页面不存在）")（英语：[Turquerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turquerie "en:Turquerie")）最早始於15世紀末，並至少持續到18世紀，包括在裝飾藝術中使用"土耳其"風格、時而採用土耳其服飾，以及對描繪[鄂圖曼帝國](/wiki/%E9%84%82%E5%9C%96%E6%9B%BC%E5%B8%9D%E5%9C%8B "鄂圖曼帝國")本身的藝術感興趣。[威尼斯](/wiki/%E5%A8%81%E5%B0%BC%E6%96%AF "威尼斯")在傳統上是[鄂圖曼帝國](/wiki/%E9%84%82%E5%9C%96%E6%9B%BC%E5%B8%9D%E5%9C%8B "鄂圖曼帝國")的貿易夥伴，是這股風潮最早的中心，而法國則在18世紀時變得更具影響力。

[中國風](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E9%A3%8E "中国风")是西歐裝飾中流行中國主題的總稱，始於17世紀末，並在多次浪潮中達到巔峰，特別是約1740-1770年間的[洛可可](/wiki/%E6%B4%9B%E5%8F%AF%E5%8F%AF "洛可可")中國風。西方設計師從文藝復興到18世紀試圖模仿中國陶瓷的技術精密性，但僅取得部分成功。早期中國風的跡象出現在17世紀中擁有活躍"東印度公司"的國家：英國（英國東印度公司）、丹麥（[丹麥東印度公司](/wiki/%E4%B8%B9%E9%BA%A5%E6%9D%B1%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E5%85%AC%E5%8F%B8 "丹麥東印度公司")）、荷蘭（[荷蘭東印度公司](/wiki/%E8%8D%B7%E8%98%AD%E6%9D%B1%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E5%85%AC%E5%8F%B8 "荷蘭東印度公司")）和法國（[法國東印度公司](/wiki/%E6%B3%95%E5%9B%BD%E4%B8%9C%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E5%85%AC%E5%8F%B8 "法国东印度公司")）。從17世紀初開始，在[臺夫特](/wiki/%E5%8F%B0%E5%A4%AB%E7%89%B9 "台夫特")和其他荷蘭城鎮製造的錫釉陶器採用真正的明代青花瓷風格。早期在[麥森](/wiki/%E8%BF%88%E6%A3%AE "迈森")和其他真瓷中心製造的陶瓷器皿模仿中國的盤、瓶、茶具形狀以及中國外銷瓷器。

具"中國風情"的遊憩涼亭出現在[巴洛克](/wiki/%E5%B7%B4%E6%B4%9B%E5%85%8B%E8%89%BA%E6%9C%AF "巴洛克艺术")晚期和洛可可時期的德國宮廷正式花園中，以及[馬德里](/wiki/%E9%A6%AC%E5%BE%B7%E9%87%8C "馬德里")附近[阿蘭胡埃斯](/wiki/%E9%98%BF%E5%85%B0%E8%83%A1%E5%9F%83%E6%96%AF "阿兰胡埃斯")的瓷磚面板上。特別是在1753年至1770年間，[湯瑪斯·齊本德爾](/wiki/%E6%B9%AF%E7%91%AA%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E9%BD%8A%E6%9C%AC%E5%BE%B7%E7%88%BE "湯瑪斯·齊本德爾")製作的紅木茶几和瓷器櫃，也常以中國式的格柵玻璃和欄杆飾件作為裝飾。早期清代文人家具的質樸風格經由轉化後被在地化。隨著"案"演變為喬治中期的側几，以及直櫺方形靠背扶手椅的出現，這類設計同時滿足英國紳士與中國文人的審美偏好與實用需求。並非所有對中國設計原則的改編都屬於主流的"中國風情"。中國風情的媒介包括模仿[漆器](/wiki/%E6%BC%86%E5%99%A8 "漆器")的[仿日漆工藝](/w/index.php?title=%E4%BB%BF%E6%97%A5%E6%BC%86%E5%B7%A5%E8%97%9D&action=edit&redlink=1 "仿日漆工藝（页面不存在）")（英语：[Japanning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanning "en:Japanning")）和彩繪錫器、早期片狀彩繪壁紙，以及陶瓷雕像和桌面擺飾。小型寶[塔](/wiki/%E5%A1%94 "塔")出現在壁爐架上，實體比例的寶塔則出現在花園中。在名為[邱](/wiki/%E9%82%B1_(%E8%8B%B1%E5%9C%8B) "邱 (英國)")的庭園有一座由[威廉·錢伯斯](/wiki/%E5%A8%81%E5%BB%89%C2%B7%E9%92%B1%E4%BC%AF%E6%96%AF "威廉·钱伯斯")設計的壯麗大寶塔。德國[司徒加特](/wiki/%E5%8F%B8%E5%BE%92%E5%8A%A0%E7%89%B9 "司徒加特")的[威廉瑪花園](/w/index.php?title=%E5%A8%81%E5%BB%89%E7%91%AA%E8%8A%B1%E5%9C%92&action=edit&redlink=1 "威廉瑪花園（页面不存在）")（英语：[Wilhelma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelma "en:Wilhelma")）（1846年）是一[摩爾復興建築](/w/index.php?title=%E6%91%A9%E7%88%BE%E5%BE%A9%E8%88%88%E5%BB%BA%E7%AF%89&action=edit&redlink=1 "摩爾復興建築（页面不存在）")（英语：[Moorish Revival architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorish_Revival_architecture "en:Moorish Revival architecture")）的例子。為藝術家[弗雷德里克·雷頓](/wiki/%E5%BC%97%E9%9B%B7%E5%BE%B7%E9%87%8C%E5%85%8B%C2%B7%E9%9B%B7%E9%A0%93 "弗雷德里克·雷頓")建造的[萊頓屋博物館](/wiki/%E8%90%8A%E9%A0%93%E5%B1%8B%E5%8D%9A%E7%89%A9%E9%A4%A8 "萊頓屋博物館")擁有傳統的外觀，但室內裝飾卻是精緻的阿拉伯風格，包括原始的伊斯蘭瓷磚和其他元素，以及維多利亞時期的東方化作品。

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Pavilion.jpg/250px-Pavilion.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](/wiki/File:Pavilion.jpg)

黃昏時分中，位於倫敦以南約76公里[布來頓](/wiki/%E5%B8%83%E4%BE%86%E9%A0%93 "布來頓")的[英皇閣](/wiki/%E8%8B%B1%E7%9A%87%E9%98%81 "英皇阁")。

歐洲和美國從1805年左右開始陷入建築異域情調的狂熱，英國的[英王閣](/wiki/%E8%8B%B1%E7%8E%8B%E9%96%A3 "英王閣")即為典型。其圓頂被認為是印度式的。1848年，表演家[菲尼亞斯·泰勒·巴納姆](/wiki/%E8%8F%B2%E5%B0%BC%E4%BA%9A%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E6%B3%B0%E5%8B%92%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E7%BA%B3%E5%A7%86 "菲尼亚斯·泰勒·巴纳姆")建造一座被認為是[蒙兀兒](/wiki/%E8%92%99%E5%85%80%E5%85%92%E5%B8%9D%E5%9C%8B "蒙兀兒帝國")風格的"伊朗斯坦"府邸，而引發美國東方風格別墅的建造熱潮。然而建築異域情調大多侷限於室內設計。火車站和泵站裝飾有摩爾式細節。城市公園裡的寶塔和拱門則採用中國或日本風格。[[34]](#cite_note-34)由於在1860年後引入[浮世繪](/wiki/%E6%B5%AE%E4%B8%96%E7%B9%AA "浮世繪")而出現[日本主義](/wiki/%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E4%B8%BB%E7%BE%A9 "日本主義")，成為對西方藝術的重要影響。特別是許多現代法國藝術家如[克洛德·莫內](/wiki/%E5%85%8B%E6%B4%9B%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E8%8E%AB%E5%85%A7 "克洛德·莫內")和[愛德加·竇加](/wiki/%E6%84%9B%E5%BE%B7%E5%8A%A0%C2%B7%E7%AB%87%E5%8A%A0 "愛德加·竇加")都受到日本風格的影響。在法國工作的美國藝術家[瑪麗·卡薩特](/wiki/%E7%91%AA%E9%BA%97%C2%B7%E5%8D%A1%E8%96%A9%E7%89%B9 "瑪麗·卡薩特")在自己的圖像中運用日本版畫的組合圖案、平滑平面和移動透視等元素。[[35]](#cite_note-35)[詹姆士·惠斯勒](/wiki/%E8%A9%B9%E5%A7%86%E5%A3%AB%C2%B7%E6%83%A0%E6%96%AF%E5%8B%92 "詹姆士·惠斯勒")的[孔雀廳](/wiki/%E5%AD%94%E9%9B%80%E5%8E%85 "孔雀厅")繪畫展示出他如何運用日本傳統元素，是該流派中最精美的作品之一。美國[加州](/wiki/%E5%8A%A0%E5%88%A9%E7%A6%8F%E5%B0%BC%E4%BA%9E%E5%B7%9E "加利福尼亞州")[格林兄弟建築師事務所](/w/index.php?title=%E6%A0%BC%E6%9E%97%E5%85%84%E5%BC%9F%E5%BB%BA%E7%AF%89%E5%B8%AB%E4%BA%8B%E5%8B%99%E6%89%80&action=edit&redlink=1 "格林兄弟建築師事務所（页面不存在）")（英语：[Greene and Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greene_and_Greene "en:Greene and Greene")）在設計[甘迺迪住宅](/w/index.php?title=%E7%94%98%E8%BF%BA%E8%BF%AA%E4%BD%8F%E5%AE%85&action=edit&redlink=1 "甘迺迪住宅（页面不存在）")（英语：[Gamble House (Pasadena, California)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamble_House_(Pasadena,_California) "en:Gamble House (Pasadena, California)")）和其他建築時也受到日本元素的啟發。

[埃及復興建築](/wiki/%E5%9F%83%E5%8F%8A%E9%A2%A8%E6%A0%BC%E5%BB%BA%E7%AF%89 "埃及風格建築")在19世紀早期和中期流行，並作為一種小眾風格，持續到20世紀初。摩爾復興建築始於19世紀早期的德意志各邦，在建造[猶太會堂](/wiki/%E7%8C%B6%E5%A4%AA%E6%9C%83%E5%A0%82 "猶太會堂")時特別受歡迎。印度-撒拉遜復興建築是19世紀末在[英屬印度](/wiki/%E8%8B%B1%E5%B1%AC%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6 "英屬印度")興起的一種流派。

西方藝術對東方主義追求的歷史悠久。東方場景可見於[中世紀](/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E4%B8%96%E7%B4%80 "中世紀")與文藝復興藝術中，且[伊斯蘭藝術](/wiki/%E4%BC%8A%E6%96%AF%E8%98%AD%E8%97%9D%E8%A1%93 "伊斯蘭藝術")本身對西方的藝術產出有深遠且具形塑性的影響。到19世紀，東方主題隨著西方在[非洲](/wiki/%E9%9D%9E%E6%B4%B2 "非洲")與[亞洲](/wiki/%E4%BA%9E%E6%B4%B2 "亞洲")的[殖民擴張](/wiki/%E6%AE%96%E6%B0%91%E4%B8%BB%E7%BE%A9 "殖民主義")而進一步激增。

### 19世紀以前

[[编辑](/w/index.php?title=%E4%B8%9C%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E4%B9%89&action=edit&section=10 "编辑章节：19世紀以前")]

[穆罕默德二世 (奧斯曼帝國)](/wiki/%E7%A9%86%E7%BD%95%E9%BB%98%E5%BE%B7%E4%BA%8C%E4%B8%96_(%E5%A5%A7%E6%96%AF%E6%9B%BC%E5%B8%9D%E5%9C%8B) "穆罕默德二世 (奧斯曼帝國)")的肖像，傳言為[真蒂萊·貝利尼](/wiki/%E7%9C%9F%E8%92%82%E8%8E%B1%C2%B7%E8%B4%9D%E5%88%A9%E5%B0%BC "真蒂莱·贝利尼")所繪（1480 年）。

對伊斯蘭摩爾人與土耳其人（對南歐、北非與西亞[穆斯林](/wiki/%E7%A9%86%E6%96%AF%E6%9E%97 "穆斯林")群體的不精確稱呼）的描繪可見於中世紀、文藝復與巴洛克藝術中。在[早期尼德蘭繪畫](/wiki/%E6%97%A9%E6%9C%9F%E5%B0%BC%E5%BE%B7%E8%98%AD%E7%B9%AA%E7%95%AB "早期尼德蘭繪畫")的聖經場景裡，次要人物（特別是[羅馬人](/wiki/%E5%8F%A4%E7%BE%85%E9%A6%AC "古羅馬")）常被賦予異域情調的服飾，隱約反映[近東](/wiki/%E8%BF%91%E6%9D%B1 "近東")的裝束。[基督誕生](/wiki/%E5%9F%BA%E7%9D%A3%E8%AA%95%E7%94%9F "基督誕生")圖中的[東方三博士](/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%89%E5%8D%9A%E5%A3%AB "東方三博士")便是其中的焦點。一般而言，除非聖經背景的藝術作品像[真蒂萊·貝利尼](/wiki/%E7%9C%9F%E8%92%82%E8%8E%B1%C2%B7%E8%B4%9D%E5%88%A9%E5%B0%BC "真蒂莱·贝利尼")等人的作品或某些19世紀作品那樣，具備當代或[歷史主義](/wiki/%E6%AD%B7%E5%8F%B2%E4%B8%BB%E7%BE%A9 "歷史主義")的中東細節或布景，否則不被視為[東方主義](/wiki/%E6%9D%B1%E6%96%B9%E4%B8%BB%E7%BE%A9 "東方主義")。文藝復興時期的[威尼斯](/wiki/%E5%A8%81%E5%B0%BC%E6%96%AF%E5%85%B1%E5%92%8C%E5%9C%8B "威尼斯共和國")曾有一段時期對繪畫與[版畫](/wiki/%E7%89%88%E7%95%AB "版畫")中的鄂圖曼帝國描繪展現出特別興趣。曾前往[君士坦丁堡](/wiki/%E5%90%9B%E5%A3%AB%E5%9D%A6%E4%B8%81%E5%A0%A1 "君士坦丁堡")為[蘇丹](/w/index.php?title=%E8%98%87%E4%B8%B9_(%E7%A8%B1%E8%99%9F)&action=edit&redlink=1 "蘇丹 (稱號)（页面不存在）")畫像的真蒂萊·貝利尼與[維托雷·卡爾帕喬](/wiki/%E7%B6%AD%E6%89%98%E9%9B%B7%C2%B7%E5%8D%A1%E7%88%BE%E5%B8%95%E5%96%AC "維托雷·卡爾帕喬")是其中的代表。此時的描繪已較為準確，男子通常身著全白。在[文藝復興繪畫中的東方地毯](/w/index.php?title=%E6%96%87%E8%97%9D%E5%BE%A9%E8%88%88%E7%B9%AA%E7%95%AB%E4%B8%AD%E7%9A%84%E6%9D%B1%E6%96%B9%E5%9C%B0%E6%AF%AF&action=edit&redlink=1 "文藝復興繪畫中的東方地毯（页

This is a Chinese-language Wikipedia article on Orientalism (东方主义). It defines Orientalism as the imitation or depiction of the "Orient" (Eastern world) by Western writers, designers, and artists in art history, literature, and cultural studies. In 19th-century academic art, Orientalist painting was an important specialty, particularly focused on West Asia and North Africa. The article covers the following major sections:

1. **Background**: The etymology of "Orient" (from Latin "Oriēns" via Middle French, meaning "east" or "rising sun"), with references to Chaucer's "The Monk's Tale" (1375) and Aneurin Bevan's "In Place of Fear" (1952).

2. **Edward Said's Critical Study**: Since the 1970s, Orientalism has been used to describe Western condescension toward Asian and North African societies. Said's seminal 1978 book "Orientalism" (東方學) is considered the foundational work of postcolonial studies. Said argued that the West essentializes Eastern societies as static and undeveloped, constructing a fictional Oriental culture serving imperial power, and that Western society is portrayed as developed, rational, and superior. The theory builds on Antonio Gramsci's cultural hegemony and Michel Foucault's discourse theory (knowledge-power relationship). Said criticized contemporary scholars including Bernard Lewis and Fouad Ajami. The analysis extends to Techno-Orientalism and postmodern Orientalism.

3. **Art**: Orientalism in art history refers to Western artists active mainly in the 19th century who specialized in Oriental subjects based on travels in West Asia. French art critic Jules-Antoine Castagnary helped spread the term pejoratively. The Société des Peintres Orientalistes Français was founded in 1893, with Jean-Léon Gérôme (a leading academic painter opposing Impressionism) as honorary president. Artists are divided into two categories: realists who carefully depicted what they saw (e.g., Gustav Bauernfeind) and those who imagined Oriental scenes without leaving their studios. French painters Eugène Delacroix (1798-1863) and Jean-Léon Gérôme (1824-1904) are widely regarded as leading figures of the movement.

4. **Oriental Studies**: Orientalists in the late 18th to early 20th centuries were scholars specializing in the languages and literature of the Eastern world, including officials of the British East India Company who argued Arabic, Indian, and Islamic cultures should be studied as equals to European culture. This included philologist William Jones. The East India Company supported Orientalism until the 1820s when "anglicists" like Thomas Babington Macaulay and John Stuart Mill shifted toward promoting Western-style education. In the 20th century, Oriental studies transformed into Middle Eastern studies and Asian studies.

5. **Architecture and Design**: Covers various Orientalist styles including Moresque patterns, Indo-Saracenic Revival architecture, Turquerie (beginning in the late 15th century, centered in Venice), Chinoiserie (beginning in the late 17th century, peaking around 1740-1770 in Rococo), Egyptomania/Egyptian Revival, and Japonisme (introduced after 1860 through ukiyo-e prints). Notable examples include the Royal Pavilion in Brighton, England (1787-1823), the Chinese House in Potsdam's Sanssouci Park (1755-1764), the Chinese Pavilion in Sweden (1763-1769), and the Wilhelma in Stuttgart (1846, Moorish Revival). Influenced artists include Claude Monet, Edgar Degas, Mary Cassatt, and James Whistler (Peacock Room).

6. **Orientalism in East Asia**: Scholars have extended Said's analysis to China, examining how Western missionaries and diplomats constructed representations of China. Missionaries after the First Opium War (1839-1842) played significant roles in shaping Western views of China. A concept called "Sacred Orientalism" describes how missionary ethnographers like Spanish friar Juan González de Mendoza idealized Asian religions as a moral contrast to Western materialism.

7. **Islamic World**: Internal criticism of Orientalism exists; as of a 2002 estimate, about 200 books and 2,000 articles on Orientalism were written in Saudi Arabia alone.

8. **Orientalist Art Before the 19th Century**: Oriental scenes appear in medieval and Renaissance art. Venetian artists like Gentile Bellini (who painted Sultan Mehmed II's portrait, c. 1480) and Vittore Carpaccio showed particular interest in Ottoman depictions. The article also covers 19th-century French, British, American, Russian, and German Orientalist art, plus Orientalism in popular culture (music, literature, film, dance), religion (Islam), and the concept of Occidentalism and othering.

"東方主義是指東方文化，這是相對於，並對立於西方文化的概念。兩者分別代表東方與西方。" (Orientalism refers to Eastern culture as opposed to and contrasted with Western culture.)

"愛德華·薩依德表示，'東方主義是一種工具，讓西方得以在政治、經濟、文化與社會各個領域來統治東方。這種影響力不僅存在於過去的殖民時代，也延續到現在。'" (Edward Said stated that Orientalism is a tool allowing the West to rule the East politically, economically, culturally, and socially, extending from colonial times to the present.)

"薩依德寫道，在這種虛構中隱含著一種觀念，即西方社會是發達、理性、靈活且優越的。" (Said wrote that this fiction implies the notion that Western society is developed, rational, flexible, and superior.)

"在藝術史中，東方主義指的是主要活躍於19世紀的西方藝術家作品，他們專門研究東方題材，並根據19世紀在西亞的旅遊經歷來創作。" (In art history, Orientalism refers to works by Western artists mainly active in the 19th century who specialized in Oriental subjects based on their travel experiences in West Asia.)

"薩依德的的理論影響後來的文化評論，讓學界開始注意到：現代工業與科技如何進一步加深西方對東方的誤解。這種誤解體現在科技東方主義（Techno-Orientalism）或後現代東方主義（postmodern Orientalism）等現象中。" (Said's theory influenced later cultural criticism, drawing attention to how modern industry and technology deepen Western misunderstandings of the East, manifested in phenomena like Techno-Orientalism and postmodern Orientalism.)

You are tasked with summarizing the raw content of a webpage retrieved from a web search. Your goal is to create a summary that preserves the most important information from the original web page. This summary will be used by a downstream research agent, so it's crucial to maintain the key details without losing essential information.

Here is the raw content of the webpage:

<webpage_content>
《二十一世紀》網絡版 二○○二年六月號 總第 3 期 2002年6月29日 跨文化實踐中的東方主義話語 ⊙ 張興成 「東方主義」（Orientalism）話語觸及到當今世界政治、經濟、文化和意識形態衝突中的諸 多問題，成為討論殖民時代和殖民時代以後全球狀態的關鍵詞。 漢語學界對於「東方主義」問題的討論已經很多，但主要停留在兩個層面，一是對薩義德 （Edward W. Said）思想的引介，二是用東方主義理論剖析中國當代的一些文化現象（如影 視、美術和留學生文學）。論者大多是將「東方主義」作為一種靜止凝固的思想或批評模式 加以接受和運用，其中不乏深刻的、頗富啟示性的討論，但研究依然十分有限。本文企圖沿 著薩義德的問題意識對「東方主義」話語作進一步的思考，從東方與第三世界批評的角度來 審視東方主義思維模式、權力運作邏輯和話語策略的演變，在跨文化實踐中來探討東方主義 話語的多維層面和流動的歷史意蘊，尤其是它從第一世界到第三世界、從宗主國到受殖者的 「理論旅行」（traveling theory）中的演變圖景。 「東方人的東方主義」 薩義德的東方主義強調了他者問題中的單向書寫一面，即西方怎樣生產東方他者形象的問 題，這是由他的批判目標所決定的。如果我們將薩義德的問題進一步延伸拓展，站在東方的 角度來看「東方主義」的消費與流通，可以提出這樣的問題：東方主義是歐美發展的、爾後 拋向「東方」的一個自治產物，抑或是歐美與亞洲之間一種擴展中的關係的產物？德里克 （Arif Dirlik）認為這是理解東方主義及其在現代性中的位置的根本1。他認為，歐美東方 主義的認知和方法在二十世紀已經成為了東方「自我形象的構成」。東方主義原本表示亞洲 社會與歐美社會之間的一種疏離，現在，隨著亞洲社會以全球資本主義的能動參與者的身份 出現，它似乎表達全球現代性內部的諸種差異了。在此掩蓋之下，東方主義為衝突的意識形 態之間的競爭提供了場所，而這些意識所效忠的中性力量已不再容易辨別出是東方的或西方 的，中國的或非中國的了2。基於此，德里克提出一個明確的概念：「東方人的東方主義」， 探討東方社會的知識份子是怎樣促成了作為實踐和概念的東方主義的出現的。 對此，岩淵功一在〈共犯的異國情調──日本和它的他者〉一文中提出了一些頗富啟示性的 闡述。該文主要探討了日本國內的日本學如何利用來自西方（主要是美國）的他者塑形，在 一種「自我東方論述」（self-orientalism）中獲利。岩淵證明了他者形象與被他者化的民 族─國家主流意識形態達成一種默契──「共犯」。 岩淵在文章一開始就提出：誰在想像建構「日本特性」？是東方主義、西方主義 （Occidentalism）還是日本的「自我東方論述」？很顯然，這一提問是在全球化語境中延伸 了「東方主義」話題。他者形象並非《東方學》（Orientalism）中那種單向的指認與強制命 名，「西方對日本的東方論述，支持著『日本特性』的建構和維持；而日本亦透過成功地利 用與『西方』的差異，自我建構了『日本特性』，這就是梅拿（Miller）所說的『自我東方 論述』」3。這種「自我東方論述」雖然也建構了一套關於「西方」的論述，但它不同於薩義 德所反對的作為回應東方主義的西方主義，因為日本的自我東方論述缺乏支配西方的力量， 它所述及的是它自己，而西方所述及的是其他者。但日本這種自我東方論述絕非一種被動反 應，它通過「利用東方論述的凝視（Orientalist gaze）把自己轉化為他者」，從而與東方 主義構成一種「淵深的共謀」，兩者都是用「他者」去本質化「自我」，鎮壓內部不同的聲 音4： 這種看法打開了民族之內和之間知識／權力聯盟的一種向度，「指出」非人化之他者的論述 建構如何被權力集團利用，以灌輸民族主義情緒進入人民的思想當中，以及透過把「我們」 相對「他們」這一種意象的論述齊一化，如何壓抑民族之內的各種不同聲音。 在現代化過程中，日本權力集團可以利用「日本特性」這樣的東方主義論述，作為動員群眾 的一種重要手段，將國家利益（主要是集團利益）極大化，並限制個人意志，個體在一個 「想像的共同體」認同中盡忠盡孝。如1910年代日本就曾以「家」為意識形態，強調日本民 族和公司如家一般，將社會衝突與異見歸為「西方病」，而忠於集體（家）的「日本特性」 理所當然地成為抑制個體對「民主」與人權的訴求。日本的「自我東方論述」帶有「非常選 擇性的操控和壓抑性質」，它還壓制了國內其他少數族群和女性、工人階級的聲音，「自我 東方論述隱藏了日本的特殊主義（Particularism）在日本內部起著統識作用的事實」5。因 此，「東方主義」融化為日本「傳統的發明打造」（invention of tradition），與日本鎮 壓異見合謀。 日本的自我東方論述與東方主義合謀更重要的在於二者從來沒發生過衝突，因為日本的自我 東方論述始終是在將西方定義為普世適用的參照點上運作的，也就是說它始終沒有脫離西方 的東方論述的邏輯軌道。二十世紀70年代以來，在「走向世界」的口號號召下，日本將普遍 主義與特殊主義、國族主義與國際主義相互發明，相互強化。「國際主義掩飾和嘗試吸納所 有的本地多元紛雜性質，而國族主義則減少國際主義的威脅和使它更令人喜愛。」6 這樣， 日本的「他者」成為跨／國族主義的共同消費品，「異色餐點」（exotic cuisine）與傳統 主義同台獻藝，日本通過「他者」，將「西方」與傳統同時本土化了。同時，日本必然以同 樣的邏輯（東方主義）去對待其他非西方國家，從而發展出一套「日本的東方主義」。它照 搬東方主義的權力等級和支配關係，成為一個「非西方的帝國主義力量」，這就是石原慎太 郎等人宣揚「日本可以說不」的本質。日本這種對東方主義的利用將東方學的「西方─東 方」模式拓展為「西方─日本─其餘」的三分對立關係，當然其本質沒有超越二元對立關 係，因為「日本的東方主義」並未改變東方主義的本質與權力邏輯。這一關係的拓展可以看 作是全球化語境中權力關係的複雜化結果。這一結構模式也可以作為一套闡釋符碼，用來分 析帶種族主義傾向的任何一個民族─國家的文化策略。 其實，酒井直樹對這一問題作過更深入的理論辨析。酒井將現代性問題納入到歷史─地緣政 治的對應角度，指出西方─現代性─普遍主義與非西方─前現代性（或仿現代性）─特殊主 義的對立思維模式如何建構了現代性神話與陷阱。東方主義無疑是構成西方現代性普世主義 觀念的重要組成部分。西方通過將自我普世化而將他者特殊化的方式，確立自我中心地位與 支配異己的目的 7： 西方永遠不滿足於他體（other）所認識的西方，它總是迫切地要求去接近自己的他體，以便 不斷地改造自我形象，它不斷地在它與他者（the other）的交往之中尋找自己；它永遠不會 滿足於被認識，相反，它卻寧可去認識他體；它寧願做認識的提供者而不做認識的接受者。 要言之，西方必須代表普遍性的契機，在這個契機之下，所有特殊性被揚棄。誠然，西方本 身就是一個特殊性，但是它卻作為一個普遍的參照係數，按照此參照係數所有他者能夠識別 出自己是個特殊性，在這一點上，西方以為自己是無所不在的。 東方主義建構的「他者」可以說是西方普遍主義意識的產物與陪襯，不過這種普遍主義是西 方特殊主義自我中心意識的膨脹，他們自以為自己代表著普遍立場。以現代化理論為普遍主 義理念，不管其實質是歐洲化還是美國化，都是「自認為普遍主義的特殊主義」，酒井認為 「某種地方主義（provincialism）和對普遍主義的渴望是一枚硬幣的兩個側面。特殊主義普 遍主義不是二律背反（antinomy）而是相輔相成的。……我們正常情況下稱之為普遍主義的 東西是一個自認為普遍主義的特殊主義，很值得懷疑普遍主義究竟有沒有可能以別的方式存 在」8。 因此，酒井通過對「別的方式」，即「日本─西方─其他」之間權力關係的內在方法論策略 的批判達到了對西方現代性「普遍主義」的質疑。自明治開國以來到鈴木大松的日本學者， 一直將日本文明視為相對於西方普遍主義文明的特殊主義，但是它對待周邊的其他文明卻以 自己為普遍文明價值自居，從而在與西方的東方主義合謀中，製造了亞洲其他文明，尤其是 中國文明作為特殊性因而有待「改造」的理論，並以此支持其二十世紀30年代聖戰的「現代 化解放」論。在這場戰爭中，日本道德被證明為普遍主義而中國道德被證明為特殊主義，中 日戰爭作為一場「道德戰爭」，日本代表著改造者而中國則是改造的對象。這樣，日本製造 了一套針對中國的「日本人的東方主義」，而其理論來源卻正是西方的現代化理論。「促使 他們（日本學者）這樣做的遠遠不是一種反西方的決心而是追隨現代化道路的意志。只要中 心化和同一化是現代化的組成部分，他們的世界歷史哲學理論便會證明多個中心並不存在， 從而自相矛盾地表明戰爭是不可避免的。」9 所以酒井指出，日本始終生活在西方的陰影 中，批判西方應該從日本開始，「對日本的批判也涉及到對西方的根本批判」10。因此酒井 贊同竹內好的觀點：「現代性是強加給非西方的……東方只有等到它變成了西方的對象的時 候才開始進入現代時期。因此，對非西方來說，現代性的真諦就是它對西方的反應……」11 這種「反應」不管是模仿還是對抗，酒井透過竹內好的論述表達了一種蒼涼的感喟：即使是 抵抗也逃不脫現代性的圈套。 華倫斯坦（Immanuel Wallerstein）認為，現代世界的民族主義並非成功的往昔文明。它們 是既想同化為普遍性，同時又想固守特殊性，即重新發明差異這種要求的模糊表達。它是經 由特殊主義到達的普遍主義和經由普遍主義到達的特殊主義12。這在一定程度上切中了文化 民族主義權力運作的基本邏輯。在今天「差異」成為了一種權力，文化民族主義的基本策略 就是要讓「差異」成為一種普遍的認同，以特殊性自居，通過東方主義式的權力運作方式確 立自我與他者之間的區分與定位，在一種傑姆遜（Fredric Jameson）意義上的後現代消費主 義的「懷舊」潮流中發明傳統，而不是發現傳統。這樣，文化民族主義在東西二元區分的同 時，有可能將「西方」與「傳統」同時本質化、他者化。更為重要的是，東方主義同樣可能 成為受殖者、第三世界民族國家之間權力爭奪的策略與手段。在這個過程中，西方既是它們 攻擊的對象，也是它們利用的神祇，因而，對西方的反抗隱含著以「西方」來對抗西方的悖 論式的方式。 所以，「東方人的東方主義」實際上是一個多重角色，它鞏固了兩種霸權形式，它通過自我 東方主義化而自動本質化（self-essentialization），一方面因內化了東方主義的歷史前提 而鞏固了「西方」的意識形態霸權，另一方面又通過確立民族主義敘事的合法性權威地位而 成為壓制國內差異的內部霸權，即一種「內部殖民」。同時，它還有第三重角色，即「東方 人的東方主義」還將東方主義文化霸權衍化為東方人或第三世界民族國家之間權力爭奪的話 語策略，從而使東方主義問題進一步複雜化、頑固化。它鼓舞了一種民族主義文化是一股現 代化力量的意識形態，主張在全球化語境中現代化途徑的多元性與獨特性，但其基本邏輯仍 然沒能脫離「把資本主義作為歷史的終結的一種目的論之中」。所以「更重要的是質疑資本 主義現代性（不僅僅是歐洲中心主義）的前提，東方主義是這種現代性的必然表現。新近對 歐洲中心主義的挑戰已經同化了資本主義的目的論（如儒學的復興），促進了而非取代了東 方主義。現在要做的是拒斥歷史目的論的一切表現。……這要求不僅要質疑大陸的區別（東 方／西方），而且要質疑作為分析單位的民族，因為後者也興起於文化的同質化和物 化」13。 透過「東方人的東方主義」，我們可以說薩義德的東方主義既是一個起點也是一個終點。說 它是起點，是因為薩義德主要講了故事的一半14，他有力地批判了東方主義的生產，而忽略 了東方人是如何消費和再生產東方主義的。說它是終點，是說東方主義不管在西方人那裡還 是在東方人那裡，其基本的權力運作邏輯和問題癥結並未發生改變，甚至隨著全球化和世界 權力爭奪的加強而變本加厲。西方也許是問題的原因，但不是全部結果，批判東方主義不能 將責任一勞永逸地拋向「西方」，對自我文化民族主義的批判就是對東方主義更徹底的批 判。 「第三世界批評」的東方主義邏輯 自二十世紀80年代中期以來，「第三世界批評」一直是全球文化討論中的重要話題，沿著 「東方人的東方主義」問題邏輯，從「第三世界批評」的角度來進一步審理東方主義權力運 作方式，有利於加深我們對東方主義在當今文化研究中的角色的理解。 傑姆遜的〈處於跨國資本主義時代中的第三世界文學〉在第三世界得到廣泛回應。其中譯文 於1989年底發表在《電影藝術》第六期上，很快就在國內形成了有關「第三世界文學」的討 論與爭鳴15。傑姆遜的文章中充滿了東方學的論述邏輯。阿赫默德（Aijaz Ahmad）敏銳地指 出傑姆遜在論述「第三世界文學」的文本生產方式時，採取了一種粗暴的單一決定論，將 「第三世界文學」統統規劃為民族主義與政治意識形態統一力量的結果。文學文本是以一種 高度差異化的方式寫成的，產生於相互爭論的多種語境和複雜的意識形態，傑姆遜的總體化 指認無疑是對「第三世界文學」的「東方化」與本質化16。 傑姆遜這種做法並非單一的現象，博埃默（Elleke Boehmer）指出，這實際上是後結構主義 和後殖民批評家可能犯的一個通病，它使我們清晰地看到來自第三世界的文學與來自第一世 界的理論之間存在著一種「相互依存關係」。將「第三世界文學」看作是由統一歷史力量所 界定的、自成一體的知識領域的傾向，結果造成「西方的後殖民批評，又重新產生一種可以 追溯到殖民時期的不平衡的話語格局：一種把宗主國的觀念結構投射到全球其他地方的話語 格局」17。一邊是西方普遍主義意義上的理論，另一邊是「第三世界」提供的文化產品與現 象。「第三世界文學」就成為一個整體的、同質化的歷史產物而被西方理論重新編碼、塑 形，這是一種典型的東方主義。「與東方學一樣，後帝國的批評話語在對待其他文化的多樣 性和神秘性時，也會蠻橫地搞包容一切的專制主義那一套。從它自封的中心出發，這種話語 只拿取為自己的理論目的服務的東西，凡是認為『無從理解的』就棄置不顧。」18後結構主 義後現代理論在移民文學身上大談邊緣性、雜交性、含混性以及對二元對立的消解等等，不 過是作為自我理論的印證，作為批判啟蒙話語的工具，而對真正的移民文學、第三世界文學 作為其「具體實在的文化和歷史（一種或多種）的產物」的理解，幾乎是不可能的，他們不 過是將「本來非常不同國家的寫作放在同一個鍋子裡煮了」19。「後現代的差異觀念和具有 肯定價值的邊緣性本身，當被第一世界的批評家用來批評第三世界文學時，可以（以更加隱 蔽的方式）重複殖民化的統治策略：其利益和關懷為帝國主義所盜用的確切點恰恰是爭論的 熱點」20。 中國二十世紀90年代的「第三世界批評」雖然問題是從西方借來的，但討論主要發生在本土 與「域外」的中國知識份子之間，即處於西方第一世界的中國學者與大陸學者之間的論爭。 有趣的是在這個論爭過程中，「域外」的學者不自覺地扮演了「西方」的角色，站在一種普 遍主義立場，對大陸的相關問題進行「家長式」的指責；而大陸學者往往以本土經驗自居， 張揚一種民族經驗的認識論優先權與問題切身性，批評「域外」學者的「洋涇」英語與隔 靴搔癢式的批評困境21。也許問題是，「域外」學者對內時秉承了西方老大的口吻，但他們 在第一世界發言時，不是經常以第三世界的特殊經驗自居嗎？同樣，大陸一些「後」學者在 面對域內其他話語時，有時不又讓人覺得是在扮演西方普遍主義角色嗎？在這變動不居的東 方主義權力運作邏輯中，我們很難分清誰是真正的「第三世界」發言者。 因此，對「第三世界批評」的東方主義邏輯可以做出如下的認識： 在「第三世界批評」中，「第三世界」仍然是西方世界「強大」的陪襯、欲望的飛地與「他 者」。同時，這一敘事邏輯承襲了東西方、現代性與前現代性等二元對立原則，從而置落後 的貧窮的民族國家於資本主義現代化目的論之中，為第三世界知識份子成為維護這一霸權的 「共犯」提供了契機。 作為「差異」角色的「第三世界」未得到進一步的差異化，而是被粗暴地劃入了統一的同質 的受支配角色。因此，這裡的「第三世界」概念在後殖民批評中常常掩蓋了內部社群、階 級、種族、區域文化之間的複雜多樣性以及它們相互之間的矛盾衝突。東方主義在地緣政治 學的粗糙劃分中，實際上掩蓋了一系列複雜的問題。隨著全球化的深入，階級、種族等等問 題也在急劇地複雜化，在第一世界內也會出現「第三世界」，而在第三世界內也會出現「第 一世界」。這也正是英國社會學家斯克萊爾（Leslie Sklair）發出的疑問，在跨國主義的全 球化中，當許多理論宣稱一個國家剝削另一個國家時：「難道這意味著即使那些生活在北美 的窮人也在剝削生活在南美的富人嗎？」22 事實上，一旦「差異」從文化走向政治，其危險性就更大。薩義德認為中東問題就是一個例 子23： 差異會成為一種意識形態傳染病。……這個世界已經被大量的社會經濟問題和大量的對此具 有阻止作用的種種意識形態和信條所包圍。而這些意識形態和信條中的大多數，卻被欺騙、 詭詐和對真理的十足的蔑視掩蓋起來了。中東很少像現在這樣顯得如此的幫派化和分裂化， 在錯綜的死氣沉沉的政治背景下，猶太復國主義、排外主義以及形形色色的反動的民族主 義，都在上面簽著自己的名字。 因此，「第三世界批評」的背後驅動力到底是甚麼，每一個文化批評者必須有清醒的認識。 德里克認為，最重要的是當今第三世界已經不再是為早期「民族解放」口號而鬥爭，「民族 解放構想不再創造別樣的社會形態，而是創造別樣的資本主義形式」24。從這個意義上看， 「第三世界文化批評」的實質就可能是「資本主義的不同文化」的論爭，由之而興起的「文 化民族主義」就可能成為資本主義全球化的推動器而不是阻礙物。這很容易陷入亨廷頓 （Samuel P. Huntington）的論斷：「在諸文明的政治中，非西方文明的各民族和各政府不 再是作為西方殖民主義目標的歷史客體，而是與西方一起成為歷史的推動者和型構 者。」25因此，以民族特色為口號的「第三世界批評」成為進入資本主義世界的合法化依據 與必然策略，一方面張揚民族主義可以成為抵抗資本主義全球化帶來的抹平趨勢的最好藉 口；另一方面由文化民族主義帶來的自給自足或尋找自我現代化路徑的口號成為加入現代資 本主義世界體系最富吸引力的一種權力運作方式26： 建構民族本質的目的是將融入全球資本主義的行為合法化；或者說，是為了證明民族文化與 加入資本主義經濟在本質上是一致的，即便不是必然要求。近年來，文化民族主義討論與資 本主義的民族文化討論不可分割。激進的理論排斥一切本質主義，實踐中卻將民族文化本質 化，這表明在我們的時代，激進的理論與世俗的政治實踐之間的鴻溝。說得更準確些，第三 世界主義拋棄了從前的民族解放目標，把民族文化加以新法西斯主義的具體化；不再為資本 主義對世界的建構提供別樣選擇，反而在全球範圍內將資本主義合法化，並復活了法西斯主 義。 結語：「理論旅行」中的東方主義問題 東方主義話語在激活了一系列問題的同時，可能掩蓋、加深了更多的問題。通過東方主義的 權力邏輯演變過程，我們可以看到霸權依然存在，甚至變本加厲，只是改變了一種名稱或口 號，因此，應該避免遺漏了更多的問題而滑入更多的理論盲點。 任何以反「東方論述」為名的文化民族主義傾向必然走向文化自戀與文化自禁的境地，同時 還會掩蓋自我內部問題，而將一切癥結拋給「西方」。「能以別人的眼光來審查自我」，但 「異我指涉」永遠不能代替「自我指涉」，西方的東方表述常常來自他們自身的問題與需 要，雖然不一定必然建立在歐洲中心主義基礎之上。從這個角度看，杜維明等人將「文化中 國」的周邊線劃在國際漢學家身上，有一定的合理性，至少可以使我們能通過他者來審視自 己，在一種「文化間性」中來理解中國問題。但必須注意的是，漢學家的研究是否真正站在 中國處境和問題上來討論「中國」。應該強調第三世界發言必須從特殊性開始，但又必須超 越特殊性。差異不能成為一種新的霸權，一種薩義德所說的「意識形態傳染病」。中國「現 代性」問題的提出、形成的方式以及它的病理現象都不僅僅只是中國內部問題，也不僅僅只 是外來文化移植，「而是在不同的文化和語言共同體之間的互動關係中形成的」27。因此， 不能將中國現代性問題看成是被動的反應，必須看到中國的文化歷史自主性進程。從這個意 義上講，二十世紀90年代中國文化民族主義的復興或「國學復興」中的問題是多層面的，既 有對「西化」、「後殖民化」的反抗，也有現代化的自我路徑探尋或尋找「另一種資本主義 現代形式」的思路。事實上，二十世紀90年代對中國近現代文化保守主義人物（如王國維、 辜鴻銘、梁漱溟、陳寅恪等人）的激烈討論本身就透露出對「中國問題」的多面性價值取向 與提問角度，很顯然，單純的文化民族主義式指責是過份簡單化了。因此，應該區分「東方 人的東方主義」內部的多種聲音，東方主義策略與結構可能是比較穩定的，但使用者和使用 的方式不同，其性質與結果就截然不同，從而使問題更複雜化、語境化。「西方─中國」與 「傳統─現代」是相輔相成的。以中國為對象，以西方為方法；以現代為尺度，以傳統為資 源；從「呼喚現代化」到「反思現代性」，展示了當今文化討論的多維視角。 透過東方主義問題，我們有必要強調跨文化、跨語際研究的重要性，既要研究西方世界的 「東方學」，也要研究中國語境中的「西方學」。西方人出於他們的問題與需要創造了「東 方學」，同樣東方人是怎樣引入、利用、闡釋與再闡釋「西方」呢？尤其是近現代以來，西 方文藝思潮的湧入與中國語境的接受達成了怎樣的關係？透過西方的東方論述，中國人是怎 樣想像現代「中國」的？或許，本文對「東方人的東方主義」的探討僅僅是粗淺地涉及到這 至將來的，都必須加以批判與檢審。「換言之，問題不是東方主義，而是東方主義在不同社 會和政治環境中的力量及其具體含義」28。 註釋 1；24；26；28 德里克（Arif Dirlik）著，王寧等譯：《後革命氛圍》（北京：中國社會科學出版 社，1999），頁278；72；73；288-89。 2 德里克：〈世界體系分析和全球資本主義〉，《戰略與管理》，1997年第1期。 3；4；5；6 This article, published in the June 2002 issue of 《二十一世紀》(Twenty-First Century) journal, is a scholarly essay by Zhang Xingcheng (張興成), a lecturer at Southwest Normal University in Chongqing, exploring the concept of "Orientalism discourse in cross-cultural practice." The author extends Edward Said's critique of Orientalism to examine how Orientalist modes of thinking and power dynamics have traveled from the First World to the Third World, and from colonizers to the colonized.

The article is structured around three main sections:

**1. "The Orientalist's Orientalism" (東方人的東方主義):** Zhang examines how non-Western societies have internalized and reproduced Orientalist discourse. Drawing on Arif Dirlik's concept, the essay argues that Orientalism has become part of Asia's "self-image construction." Key examples include:
- Japan's "self-orientalism" (as analyzed by Koichi Iwabuchi), where Japanese scholars used Western Orientalist discourse to construct "Japaneseness" while suppressing internal dissent, minority voices, and women's rights. This "self-Orientalism" operated in collusion with Western Orientalism, never challenging its basic logic.
- Naoki Sakai's theoretical analysis showing how Japan constructed its own "Japanese Orientalism" toward other Asian nations (particularly China), using Western modernization theory to justify its imperialist wars in the 1930s, positioning Japan as universalist and China as particularist.
- The conclusion that "Orientalism by Orientals" serves multiple roles: reinforcing Western ideological hegemony through self-essentialization, establishing internal hegemony (internal colonization) by suppressing domestic differences, and becoming a discursive strategy for power struggles among Third World nations.

**2. "The Orientalist Logic of Third World Criticism":** The article analyzes how "Third World criticism" often reproduces Orientalist logic. Key points include:
- Fredric Jameson's essay on Third World literature is criticized for homogenizing diverse Third World texts into nationalist allegories, an Orientalizing gesture identified by Aijaz Ahmad.
- Poststructuralist and postcolonial critics (per Elleke Boehmer and Linda Hutcheon) risk re-creating colonial-era discursive imbalances by treating Third World literature as raw material for Western theory.
- The article notes the irony that Chinese scholars in the West sometimes adopt a "Western" universalist stance toward mainland Chinese scholars, while claiming Third World particularity when speaking in the West.
- Dirlik's warning that "Third World criticism" may actually serve to legitimize capitalism globally rather than offer alternatives, with cultural nationalism potentially becoming an engine (rather than obstacle) for capitalist globalization.

**3. Conclusion on "Theorizing Travel":** Zhang concludes that Orientalist power logic persists even as it changes names and slogans. He argues that cultural nationalism reacting against Orientalism risks cultural narcissism, self-enclosure, and scapegoating the West. He emphasizes the importance of cross-cultural and cross-linguistic research, distinguishing different voices within "Orientalist Orientalism," and stresses that the central question is not Orientalism itself but "the power of Orientalism in different social and political environments and its concrete meanings" (citing Dirlik). He calls for critical examination of all cultural hegemony, whether Eastern or Western, First World or Third World, internal or external.

--- SOURCE 1: Postcolonialism and Orientalism: Said, Spivak, Bhabha, and the Critique of Colonial Discourse | Philosophy in Summary — Thinkers & Syntheses ---
URL: https://filosofiaemresumo.com.br/en/artigos/postcolonialism-orientalism-said-spivak-fanon

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage provides a comprehensive survey of postcolonial theory, tracing its precursors and key figures who consolidated the field. The article covers four main thinkers and the critical debates surrounding postcolonial theory.

**Precursors:**
- W. E. B. Du Bois (1868–1963), an African-American sociologist, formulated "double consciousness" in *The Souls of Black Folk* (1903)—the inner experience of seeing oneself through others' eyes, divided between being American and Black. He also coined the "color line" thesis, arguing that racial boundaries (not just class) structure modern world politics.
- Frantz Fanon (1925–1961) analyzed colonized subjects' internalization of negative self-images in *Black Skin, White Masks* (1952), showing colonialism as a psychic and ontological wound, not merely economic/political domination.

**Key Theorists:**
- **Edward Said** (1935–2003), Palestinian-American critic at Columbia, founded postcolonial studies with *Orientalism* (1978). Drawing on Foucault's power/knowledge and Gramsci's hegemony, he argued "the Orient" is a Western discursive construction—an essentialized, backward, feminized Other that authorizes Western governance. He introduced "imaginative geographies" and later "contrapuntal reading" in *Culture and Imperialism* (1993).
- **Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak** (b. 1942), Derrida's translator, combined deconstruction, Marxism, and feminism. Her canonical essay "Can the Subaltern Speak?" (1988) argued the subaltern's intelligibility is blocked by colonial and national representational codes. Using the example of *sati* (widow self-immolation), she showed the subaltern woman faces two competing representations (British "white men saving brown women from brown men" vs. Indian patriarchy), neither allowing her to speak. She coined "epistemic violence" and "strategic essentialism" (from which she later distanced herself).
- **Homi Bhabha** (b. 1949), author of *The Location of Culture* (1994), shifted focus to ambivalence in colonial relations. His concepts include "hybridity" (no culture remains pure), "mimicry" (colonial imitation that is "almost the same, but not quite," exposing colonial fragility), and the "third space" (interstitial site of cultural negotiation transcending binaries).

**Critiques and Debates:**
- Marxist critics like Aijaz Ahmad (*In Theory*, 1992) charged postcolonial theory with privileging discourse over political economy and class, and with being a comfortable product of the Western academy written by diasporic intellectuals.
- Latin American decolonial thought (Quijano, Mignolo, Dussel) differs by locating modernity/coloniality's origin in 1492 rather than 19th–20th century imperialism, and calling for a more radical epistemic break with European categories.

**Essential readings** listed include works by Du Bois, Fanon, Said, Spivak, Bhabha, and Ahmad. The article concludes that thinking the colonial inheritance is a condition of honest reflection on culture, identity, and power.

--- SOURCE 4: What is Third Space? | Definition, Examples, & Analysis ---
URL: https://www.perlego.com/knowledge/study-guides/what-is-third-space

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This Perlego study guide, authored by Dr. Sophie Raine (PhD, English Literature, Lancaster University), published 05.08.2024, provides a comprehensive overview of the concept of "third space" in critical theory, sociology, and discrimination/race relations.

**Core Definition & Origins:** The concept of third space is attributed to postcolonial scholar Homi K. Bhabha (in *The Location of Culture*, 1994). It refers to a site of cultural hybridity where multiple cultures intersect, creating new cultural identities. These interstitial spaces arise from the colonizer/colonized dynamic and serve as sites of resistance where marginalized individuals (colonial subjects) can negotiate, transform, and redefine identities imposed by dominant cultural discourses. Key example: the dissemination of the English Bible in India, which resulted in a reinterpretation creating a space neither entirely English nor Indian. Physical examples include festivals, migrant-run restaurants, and the US-Mexico borderlands.

**Third Space in Postcolonial Studies:** Bhabha links third space to hybridity—Amar Acheraïou notes "hybridity is the third space." Third spaces are "liminal and interstitial sites where cultural meaning is not simply reflected but actively produced." Bhabha gives physicality to the concept through the Gacaca, a traditional Rwandan meeting space for post-genocide adjudication between Tutsis and Hutus, described as a "site of in-betweenness" between accused and accuser. Bhabha also examines a passage from Conrad's *Heart of Darkness* where a "white worsted" thread around a dying native's neck illustrates the third space—a commodity of colonial trade rendered untranslatable in the colonial context. Related theorists include Edward Said (*Orientalism*, 1978) on the "Orient" as a Western-created idea, and Gloria Anzaldúa (*Borderlands/La Frontera*, 1987) on borderlands as hybrid cultural spaces.

**Edward Soja's Thirdspace:** Soja applied Bhabha's concept to urban geography in *Thirdspace* (1996), drawing on Henri Lefebvre's "spatial triad" (*The Production of Space*, 1974): spatial practice (physical city space), representations of space (official/administrative conceptions), and spaces of representation (inhabitants' cultural understanding). Soja delineates three types: Firstspace (real/physical), Secondspace (imagined/conceived), and Thirdspace (hybrid of real and imagined). Using a market as example: firstspace is geographic location, secondspace is how planners conceive it, thirdspace is lived space where communities socialize. Soja coined "critical thirding as othering"—a rejection of either/or binary thinking (subject-object, male-female, black-white, etc.). Smagorinsky notes thirdspace focuses on how least affluent, privileged people inhabit and ascribe meaning to place.

**Third Space Feminism:** Feminist scholars have explored third spaces as sites for women to resist traditional roles. Golnaraghi and Daghar analyze how online third spaces allow Muslim women to renegotiate identities beyond Orientalist and traditionalist Islamic binaries (e.g., the 2013 "Somewhere in America #Mipsterz" video). Marissa Vigneault discusses Hannah Wilke's *S.O.S. Starification Object Series* (1974-1982) and the #MeToo movement as third-space resistance. Adela C. Licona's *Zines in Third Space* examines feminist-of-color zines (e.g., Mimi Nguyen's *Evolution of a Race Riot* 1997; Jackie Wang's *Memoirs of a Queer Hapa* 2007) as third-space radical rhetorical performances.

**Concluding Thoughts:** Shehrazade Emmambokus developed "Overlapping Space," fusing Third Space, diaspora space, and translation (focused on second-generation migrants). Third space theory has practical applications including LGBTQ+ inclusive curriculums (Steven P. Camicia's *Critical Democratic Education and LGBTQ-Inclusive Curriculum*, 2016). The concept now serves as a framework in postcolonial studies, queer theory, subaltern studies, and diaspora theory.
</summary>

The principles established at the Bandung Conference (1955), the Buenos Aires Plan of Action (PABA, 1978), and reaffirmed in the Nairobi Declaration (2009) are at risk of being discredited by SSC that replicates dominant practices, particularly since SSC remains state-centric and elite-driven, mediated by economic interests.

The authors reference Escobar's (2017) three models of cooperation: development assistance (traditional, World Bank/NGOs), cooperation as/for social justice (human rights, environmental sustainability, e.g., OXFAM), and cooperation for autonomy or solidarity cooperation linked to post-development proposals. The authors argue SSC should aim for the latter, grounded in community-level public policy proposals rather than state-level planning.

3. **The common in SSC**: The common is understood as something to be constructed from communities, not imposed. Drawing on Dardot and Laval (2015) and Torres-Galarza (2018), the common challenges the logic of the market from culture and community. The authors propose three constitutive elements for SSC: objective (well-being for all), process (total horizontality in reciprocity), and principle (solidarity and otherness).

4. **Latin American social experiences** as sources of alternative frameworks:
   - *Quilombismo* (Abdias Nascimento, Brazil): Community-based cooperative economy, collective land use, anti-racist, anti-capitalist, anti-colonialist model inspired by quilombos (maroon communities).

   - *Zapatismo* (Mexico, EZLN): Autonomy, self-government, "lead by obeying" political principle, communal decision-making.

5. **Proposed analytical framework**: The authors suggest criteria for SSC based on three moments:
   - **Principle (solidarity)**: SSC should socialize knowledge, move from appropriation-possession to appropriation-destiny, and put objects of cooperation in common; mobilizing categories of ancestry, interbeing, and pluriverse.
   - **Process (horizontality)**: SSC should be a "policy of the common" between local and global levels, develop through democratic practices, and connect global to local levels via political and social federalism; mobilizing autonomy, interculturality, and otherness.
   - **Purpose (well-being)**: SSC should build co-activity and co-obligation guided by the right to post-development, connect global plans to local needs, and establish well-being as a global common.

The chapter concludes that Latin American and Caribbean ancestral epistemological and ontological structures—relationality, community spirit, solidarity, harmony with nature, and pluriversity—are precursors to criticism of modernity and offer a research agenda for rethinking SSC as a mechanism to challenge the current world order and promote a new civilizing parameter based on the common.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Wikipedia article on "Decolonization of knowledge" (also called epistemic or epistemological decolonization), a concept in decolonial scholarship that critiques the hegemony of Western knowledge systems and seeks to construct and legitimize other knowledge systems through alternative epistemologies, ontologies, and methodologies.

**Background:** The concept inquires into historical mechanisms of knowledge production and their colonial and ethnocentric foundations. Scholars like Budd L. Hall, Jaco S. Dreyer, and Anibal Quijano argue that Western knowledge systems, which emerged during the Renaissance and Enlightenment, were deployed to legitimize European colonial endeavors and continue to "exclude, marginalise and dehumanise" those with different systems of knowledge. Linda Tuhiwai Smith's book "Decolonizing Methodologies" is a foundational text. Colonialism has ended legally and politically, but its legacy continues in "colonial situations" referred to as "coloniality."

**Origin and Development:** While rooted in resistance since 1492, its academic emergence is recent. It traces to Latin American thinkers, particularly Peruvian sociologist Anibal Quijano, who linked "coloniality of power" with "coloniality of knowledge." It developed from critical stances including postcolonialism, subaltern studies, and postmodernism, drawing on José Carlos Mariátegui, Frantz Fanon, and Immanuel Wallerstein. Political decolonization in the 20th century failed to achieve epistemological decolonization.

**Themes:** The concept involves a critique of objectivity as a colonial legacy, arguing that notions of truth and fact are "local" rather than universal. It holds that the Western knowledge system reduced epistemic diversity and suppressed other knowledge forms. Scholars like Lewis Gordon argue "knowledges" (plural) is more appropriate than "knowledge" (singular). Walter Mignolo describes the modern foundation of knowledge as territorial and imperial. Achille Mbembe says decolonization means contesting hegemonic Western epistemology.

**Significance:** Anibal Quijano argues epistemological decolonization is necessary for intercultural communication and alternative rationality. Ndlovu-Gatsheni says it addresses the "asymmetrical global intellectual division of labor" where Europe and North America produce theories consumed globally.

**Approaches:**
- **Indigenous decolonization:** Contests and reframes narratives about indigenous histories and colonial effects, adopts critical stance toward western-centric research, and seeks to reposition knowledge within Indigenous cultural practices. Some decolonial work relying on Western political thought has been criticized as paradoxically furthering dispossession.
- **Relational model of knowledge:** Louis Botha et al argue indigenous knowledges are relational, valuing relationships between actors, objects, and settings, and are fundamentally spiritual.
- **In academia:** Calls for greater representation of pluralistic ideas, inclusive curricula, expanded reading lists, and scrutiny of authority figures and epistemologies. Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o emphasizes language as the starting point of decolonization; Mahmood Mamdani argues single-language universities are a colonial heritage and advocates for multilingual, diverse academic traditions.
- **Disciplines:** Proponents call for decolonization of history, science and history of science, philosophy (especially epistemology), psychology, sociology, religious studies, legal studies, and ethnomusicology.
  - **History:** The "colonialist worldview" has impacted the field; decolonial approach examines non-Western world on its own terms.
  - **Modern science:** Contests science as "purely objective, solely empirical, immaculately rational"; critics identify scientism as an ideology rooted in the Enlightenment. Boisselle argues for a "relational science" based on "relational ontology"; Samuel Bendeck Sotillos critiques modern science's rejection of metaphysics and promotes sacred science (scientia sacra).
  - **History of science:** Since the mid-1980s, postcolonial histories seek "decentered, diasporic, or 'global' rewriting" of nation-centred imperial grand narratives, acknowledging diverse global origins of science.
  - **Philosophy:** The decolonial turn liberates reason beyond Enlightenment rationality; scholars argue for inclusion of Islamic, African, Indian, Chinese, Asian, and Latin American philosophy.
  - **Psychology:** Decolonization is "essentially a psychological project" involving "recovery of self"; seeks to show colonialism and Eurocentric presumptions are ingrained in modern psychological science, creating space for indigenous knowledge and lived experiences.
  - **Sociology:** Decolonial scholars argue the Global North dominates sociological study, portraying the Global South as "deviant" or "yet to be modernized" despite constituting ~84% of world population.

This academic article (Dados, vol. 63, no. 4, 2020, DOI: 10.1590/dados.2020.63.4.221) critiques the "coloniality of knowledge" thesis in Latin American decolonial theory. The author argues that the epistemological claims of four decolonial thinkers—Aníbal Quijano, Walter Mignolo, Enrique Dussel, and Santiago Castro-Gómez—are problematic because they are based on distorted and simplistic readings of Descartes, Hume, and other Enlightenment figures; make contentious generalizations about "Western epistemology"; and ultimately lead to epistemic relativism, which undermines the social sciences and, contrary to decolonial aspirations, renders the subaltern unable to speak.

The article proceeds through four main sections:

1. **Quijano and Mignolo on Descartes**: The author critiques Quijano's 1992 paper "Colonialidad del Poder, Eurocentrismo y América Latina" (cited over 4,400 times), which claims Cartesian subject-object epistemology enabled colonial domination and invisibilized the colonial order. The author argues Quijano provides no evidence, does not cite Descartes directly, and misreads Descartes' dualism—noting that Descartes actually describes mind and body as "so closely interrelated" that they "compose one whole," and that Cartesianism was even used by François Poulain de la Barre (1673) to defend feminism. Quijano's claims about Descartes' role in racial and gender domination are deemed unfounded. Mignolo's similar claims (e.g., that the European system of knowledge was "built on the premise that everyone in the world should believe they think and therefore exist") are likewise critiqued as shallow misreadings, since Descartes explicitly states on page two of the Discourse on Method that his aim is "not to teach the method which everyone must follow...but only to reveal how I have tried to direct my own."

2. **Dussel's liberation philosophy**: The author traces the origins of decolonial epistemological claims to Dussel's 1969 work "Para una Destrucción de la Historia de la Ética" and his influential "Philosophy of Liberation" (1977), which claims "I conquer" is the "practical foundation of 'I think'" and that the Cartesian ego cogito provided the epistemological foundation for slavery, patriarchal domination, and the capitalist wage. 3. **Castro-Gómez's "zero point" thesis**: The author critiques Castro-Gómez's "La Hybris del Punto Cero" (2005), which claims Enlightenment science was a "neutral platform for observation" that displaced local, indigenous forms of knowing and equates Spanish Jesuit racism in New Granada with the Enlightenment project as a whole. The author argues this mischaracterizes Enlightenment science, noting that many scientific findings were published in vernacular languages rather than Latin, and that scientists from Bacon, Descartes, and Galileo onward did not claim to know things in their "essence."

The author clarifies that while knowledge production is never "innocent" and colonial assumptions must be critiqued, the problematic relationship between colonialism and knowledge production is "not epistemological but political and sociological." The author defends the scientific method (as a conjunction of empiricism, rationalism, and critical realism) as a powerful valid tool, citing Susan Haack's point that "not all, and not only, scientists are reliable inquirers" and that there is no uniquely rational mode of inquiry used by all and only scientists. SUMMARY:
<summary>
This essay by Abraham Acosta, published in FORMA Journal (Vol. 1, No. 1, 2019), is a critical examination of Aníbal Quijano's concept of "coloniality of power" within decolonial theory. The author argues that despite coloniality of power's centrality to decolonial thought, little rigorous scrutiny has been applied to Quijano's own formulations. Through close reading of two of Quijano's essays—"Colonialidad y modernidad/racionalidad" (1992) and "Colonialidad de poder, cultura y conocimiento en América Latina" (1997)—Acosta contends that the coloniality of power is riddled with ambiguity and contradiction, potentially undermining its status as the theoretical bedrock of decoloniality.

Key arguments include: (1) Quijano defines colonialism broadly as "a formal system of political domination by some societies over others," which does not limit colonialism to European domination, thereby undermining decoloniality's positioning against Western modernity specifically. (2) Acosta analyzes discrepancies between the Spanish original and two English translations of Quijano's essay, noting that the 2007 republished translation (also attributed to Sonia Therborn) added the qualifier "Eurocentered" to colonialism—a modification not present in the original or the 1999 translation—revealing an attempt to resolve an irreducible ambiguity. (3) Quijano distinguishes "political colonialism" (direct subordination/coercion, drawing on Gramscian notions of domination) from "cultural colonialism" (hegemonic, ideological colonization of the dominated's imagination), with coloniality of power springing from the latter. (4) Acosta argues that cultural colonialism/coloniality of power functions merely as a synonym for hegemony and "expresses nothing more than the ideology of any reigning form of hegemonic power," failing to account for the underlying political structures of domination. (5) Quijano's broader concept of "reoriginalization"—a transhistorical dynamic of cultural transformation of which coloniality of power is but one instance—creates further problems: if all cultures have been reoriginalized at some point, then there are no truly "original" cultures (Mayan, Aztec, Incan, etc.) to reclaim, nullifying the premise of decoloniality itself. (6) Acosta concludes that coloniality of power and reoriginalization "partake of the same deep ideological grammar" and are formally indistinct from one another, meaning decoloniality—as the oppositional countermeasure to coloniality—is equally undermined. The essay ultimately questions whether one can "de-reoriginalize" at all, since coloniality of power is the innermost mechanical activity of the very transhistorical process Quijano affirms.
</summary>

"Thus colonialism, in the sense of a formal system of political domination by some societies over others seems a question of the past." (Quijano, 1999, 41)

--- SOURCE 15: Decolonising epistemologies - Alana Lentin ---
URL: https://www.alanalentin.net/2017/02/10/decolonising-epistemologies

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is the second post in Alana Lentin's "Race Critical and Decolonial Sociology" blog series, published February 10, 2017, focusing on decolonising epistemologies. The post examines the interconnections between postcolonial theory and decolonial approaches, exploring epistemological implications and possibilities for transformative social and political action.

**Postcolonial Theory**: Postcolonialism grew out of anti-colonial movements and theorizes both the legacy of European colonization and the aspiration for emancipation. Key thinkers discussed include Couze Venn (who frames postcolonialism as both postcolonial and post-occidental), Ella Shohat (questioning when the "post-colonial" begins), Gyan Prakash (arguing that both nationalism and Marxism reproduced colonial master narratives, and that postcolonial critique must "undo the Eurocentrism produced by the institution of the west's trajectory"), and Homi Bhabha (the postcolonial subject as hybrid, occupying an in-between position). The postcolonial is relational rather than territorial, with the Third World subject seen as deterritorialised and politics understood as a "politics of positionality."

**Dirlik's Critique**: Arif Dirlik offers a scathing critique of postcolonial theory, arguing it only became significant once Third World academics succeeded in the western academy. He contends that postcolonial discourse is "an expression not so much of agony over identity... but of newfound power," and that postcolonial critics generalize from local contexts to the global while denying global forces' impact on the local. Critics like O'Hanlon and Washbrook argue the focus on hybridity leads to a "depoliticising insulation of social from material domains," making postcolonialism conservative. David Macey's critique of the "post-colonial Fanon" is quoted at length—that the angry Third Worldist Fanon was replaced by one "worried about identity politics" who "is no longer angry."

**Historicism and Modernity**: Dipesh Chakrabarty's "Provincializing Europe" problematises history as a narrative of transition, showing how Indian nationalists internalised western universal presumptions. Gurminder Bhambra critiques modernisation theory as a "theory of convergence" and the multiple modernities approach for remaining Eurocentric, arguing instead that "colonisation was not simply an outcome of modernity, but, rather, modernity itself, the modern world, developed out of colonial encounters." Bhambra emphasises interrelatedness and "connected and entangled histories," exemplified by how cotton milling in Manchester depended on cotton from India.

**The Decolonial Approach**: Decolonial thinking originates mainly with Latin American scholars (Ramon Grosfoguel, Walter Mignolo, Enrique Dussel, Arturo Escobar, Gloria Anzaldua) and traces its genealogy through liberation theology, dependency theory, and Latin American autonomous social science. Unlike postcolonialism, decolonial thinkers call for "delinking" from modern colonial epistemology rather than merely deconstructing it. Mignolo states: "the rhetoric of modernity is that of salvation, whereas the logic of coloniality is a logic of imperial oppression... you cannot have modernity without coloniality."

**The Modernity/Coloniality Research Programme**: Escobar outlines five key points: (1) the conquest of the Americas as the starting point of modernity (Dussel's "first modernity"), not the Enlightenment; (2) colonialism as constitutive of modernity (Quijano's "coloniality of power"—colonial logics persisting after colonialism); (3) modernity as a worldwide process (Dussel's "transmodernity," giving voice to negated Others); (4) domination of non-Europeans as integral to modernity, with silenced knowledges; and (5) Eurocentrism as the knowledge form of modernity/coloniality.

**Impacts on the Academy**: Boaventura de Sousa Santos's "abyssal thinking" is discussed—modern knowledge and law divide social reality into visible and invisible realms, rendering indigenous and plebian knowledges nonexistent. Mignolo's "border thinking" (drawing on Gloria Anzaldua) rejects both Eurocentrism and anti-western fundamentalism, redefining concepts like citizenship, democracy, and human rights for non-western contexts, with the Zapatista movement as an example. Gender is introduced as a further power divide through Anzaldua and Maria Lugones.

A comment from Erik Ljungberg (April 19, 2019) challenges the claim that the Industrial Revolution depended on Indian cotton, noting England sourced cotton from America (citing "Empire of Cotton" by Sven Beckert), though acknowledging this doesn't change the overall argument about interconnectedness.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"the rhetoric of modernity is that of salvation, whereas the logic of coloniality is a logic of imperial oppression. They go hand in hand, and you cannot have modernity without coloniality; the unfinished project of modernity carries over its shoulders the unfinished project of coloniality." — Walter Mignolo
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 1: Latin American Dependency Theory | Global South Studies ---
URL: https://www.globalsouthstudies.org/keyword-essay/latin-american-dependency-theory

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This essay by Steven Schmidt (January 21, 2018, Global South Studies) traces the intellectual history of Latin American Dependency Theory, a political-economic school of thought that emerged from the UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) shortly after World War II. Key scholars include Raúl Prebisch, Fernando Cardoso, Enrique Faletto, and Andre Gunder Frank, with later influence on world-systems analysis by Immanuel Wallerstein, Giovanni Arrighi, and Christopher Chase-Dunn.

Dependency theory argues that under-development in Latin America is the direct result of capital intervention and global economic forces, not a "lack" of development. It emerged as a response to modernization theory (associated with economist William Rostow's five stages of economic growth), which dependency theorists rejected as a false dichotomy between "traditional" and "modern" societies.

Central to the theory is the Prebisch-Singer thesis, developed by Prebisch (former Argentine chief trade diplomat) and UN economist Hans Singer, which demonstrated through trade data that an imbalance in terms of trade caused a constant flow of capital out of Latin America—as the region exported primary goods (food, lumber, minerals) while re-importing higher-value manufactured products from the Global North, creating a perpetual trade deficit.

The theory split into two camps: (1) liberal reformers like Prebisch, Cardoso, and Faletto, who advocated for import-substitution industrialization (ISI) and protectionist policies to develop domestic markets; and (2) neo-Marxists like Gunder Frank, who argued dependency could only be escaped through socialism and challenging the capitalist mode of production. A further offshoot was world-systems analysis (Wallerstein, Amin, Frank).

During the 1940s-1950s, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, and Chile adopted ISI policies, but debt crises in the 1980s led the World Bank and IMF to impose structural adjustment programs (SAPs), which dismantled these protections. While dependency theory is no longer widely applied as policy, its core insights remain valuable: understanding how global capital flows structure development disparities, challenging assumptions that Latin American economies are "feudal and backwards," that modernity equals industrialization, and that all nations can equally pass through development "stages." The theory laid groundwork for research on the international division of labor, commodity chains, and global cities (Sassen 1991).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Dependency theory argues that under-development as experienced in Latin America and elsewhere is the direct result of capital intervention, rather than a condition of 'lacking' development or investment."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: Dependency theory - Wikipedia ---
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependency_theory

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Wikipedia article on Dependency theory, an international relations theory within the broader frameworks of imperialism studies and Marxist international relations theory. 

**Core concept:** Dependency theory posits that resources flow from a "periphery" of poor, exploited states to a "core" of wealthy states, enriching the latter at the expense of the former. The central contention is that poor states are impoverished and rich ones enriched by how poor states are integrated into the "world system." The theory was formally developed in the late 1940s following World War II as scholars sought to explain the lack of development in Latin America.

**Origins and History:** The theory arose as a reaction to modernization theory, which held that all societies progress through similar development stages. Dependency theory rejected this, arguing underdeveloped countries are not primitive versions of developed ones but have unique structures and are weaker members of the world market economy. The theory originated with two 1949 papers by Hans Singer and Raúl Prebisch, who observed deteriorating terms of trade for underdeveloped countries (the Prebisch–Singer thesis). Prebisch, an Argentine economist at the UN Commission for Latin America, advocated import-substitution industrialization (ISI) over export orientation. Paul A. Baran developed it from a Marxian perspective in 1957 with *The Political Economy of Growth*. Two main streams emerged: Latin American Structuralist (Prebisch, Celso Furtado, Aníbal Pinto) and American Marxist (Baran, Paul Sweezy, Andre Gunder Frank). The theory was popular in the 1960s-1970s as criticism of modernization theory. Walter Rodney's 1972 book *How Europe Underdeveloped Africa* applied it to Africa. Ruy Mauro Marini developed a specifically Marxist dependency theory focused on super-exploitation and unequal exchange. Fernando Henrique Cardoso (later Brazilian President 1995-2002) wrote extensively on dependency theory, developing the concept of "dependent development."

**Basic premises:** (1) Poor nations provide natural resources, cheap labor, destinations for obsolete technology, and markets for developed nations, without which the latter couldn't enjoy their standard of living; (2) Wealthy nations actively perpetuate dependence through economics, media control, politics, banking, finance, education, culture, and sport.

**Key concepts:** Baran placed surplus extraction and capital accumulation at the center of analysis, arguing that surplus in poor countries goes to luxury consumption rather than development investment. Latin American Structuralists argued for "dependent development" - partial development still controlled by outside decision-makers. Some argue the sine qua non of dependency is not technological difference but financial strength - particularly the inability of peripheral countries to borrow in their own currency, and US control of the international reserve currency (the dollar). Theotonio dos Santos described a "new dependency" based on Marxian analysis. The theory influenced world-systems theory developed by Immanuel Wallerstein, which added a third category of "semi-periphery" countries.

**Examples:** European colonization (1650-1900) of the Americas, Africa, and Asia, where wealth was transferred from colonized regions to Europe through control of materials, production, and distribution.

**Criticism:** India's economic improvement after moving to open trade is cited as evidence against the theory (though Indian economists Utsa and Prabhat Patnaik argue this may reflect a globalized reserve workforce). Import-substitution economies in Africa like Zimbabwe have performed poorly while trade-based economies like Egypt, South Africa, and Tunisia have succeeded. Economic historian Robert C. Allen argues dependency theory's claims are "debatable" because protectionism in Latin America failed, leading to excessive debt and recession, partly because national markets were too small to efficiently produce complex industrial goods.

**Other details:** The article also covers aid dependency, including instilling aid dependency, stunted economic growth, political dependency, corruption, and efforts to end aid dependency. Dependency theorists divide into liberal reformists (advocating targeted policy interventions) and neo-Marxists (proposing planned economies). The theory has lost influence with the growth of India and East Asian economies but still influences NGO campaigns like Make Poverty History and the fair trade movement.
</summary>

"Dependency theory is the idea that resources flow from a 'periphery' of poor and exploited states to a 'core' of wealthy states, enriching the latter at the expense of the former. A central contention of dependency theory is that poor states are impoverished and rich ones enriched by the way poor states are integrated into the 'world system.'"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: Remembering Dependency Theory - New Politics ---
URL: https://newpol.org/issue_post/remembering-dependency-theory

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Marxist-Humanist review article by Edward L. Tapia, published in New Politics (Summer 2017, Vol. XVI No. 3, Whole Number 63), titled "Remembering Dependency Theory." The article argues that dependency theory—a set of anti-colonial and anti-imperialist theoretical schemas that emerged after World War II—failed to properly grasp Marx's concept of value because it remained fixated on exchange value rather than penetrating into the social relations of production and abstract labor, which Tapia identifies as the defining principle of capitalism.

Key arguments and content:

1. **Origins and schools of dependency theory**: The theory emerged from anti-colonial/anti-imperialist struggles in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. It argued that global capitalist expansion generated development in core locations (Western Europe, North America, Japan) and underdevelopment in peripheral locations (Africa, Asia, Latin America). It spanned from the revolutionary socialist school (Andre Gunder Frank, Samir Amin, Theotonio dos Santos) to the bourgeois nationalist/social-democratic school (Arghiri Emmanuel, Fernando Henrique Cardoso, Enzo Faletto).

2. **Unequal exchange theory**: Dependency theorists relied on the Prebisch-Singer thesis, arguing primary commodity prices secularly fall relative to manufactured goods. They followed Ricardian theory of value, assuming commodities exchange at value and international equalization of profit rates, whereas Marx showed prices of production deviate from value due to abstract/socially necessary labor-time.

3. **Marx's counter-argument**: Marx demonstrated that advanced countries with higher organic composition of capital sell at prices of production above their value, exploiting less-advanced countries. Key quotes from Theories of Surplus Value, Grundrisse, and Capital Vol. III illustrate this—including Marx's statement that "three days of labor of one country can be exchanged against one of another country" and that "the richer country exploits the poorer one, even where the latter gains by the exchange."

4. **Industrialization and delinking strategies**: Two divergent theses emerged: "associated dependent development" (Cardoso and Faletto, involving semi-peripheral industrialization with international/local capital alliances) and "development of underdevelopment" (Frank). Both advocated "delinking"—either as mercantilist strategy to re-enter the world market later, or as disassociation toward socialism.

5. **Critique of delinking**: Tapia argues delinking fails because it addresses distribution rather than abstract value production, and socially necessary labor-time continues operating in national contexts. He cites Raya Dunayevskaya's Philosophy and Revolution on the whole human being and the persistence of the law of value.

6. **Failure of dependency theory**: It failed to anticipate the "new industrial division of labor" exemplified by the East Asian Tigers (South Korea, Taiwan) in the 1970s. The article discusses John Smith's Imperialism in the 21st Century on globalization of production (foreign direct investment and "arm's length outsourcing"), noting the global economically active population grew from 1.9 billion (1980) to 3.1 billion (2006), a 63% increase. Tapia criticizes Smith's "super-exploitation" theory as an inadequate basis for understanding imperialism, siding with Michael Roberts that exploitation is determined by the ratio of surplus value to the value of labor power.

7. **Conclusion**: Tapia calls on today's revolutionary activists to choose between building freely associated human relations that negate the law of value, or repeating the "old illusions of past socialist experiments." He cites the fates of dependency theorists—Cardoso became a neoliberal Brazilian president, Amin remained a self-declared Maoist, and Frank argued capitalism and socialism never existed.

The article includes a substantial bibliography of works by Amin, Anderson, Birkan, Carchedi, Roberts, Cardoso/Faletto, Dunayevskaya, Evans, Frank, Grossman, Hudis, Marx, Pieterse, Pradella, and Smith.
</summary>

In this case, the richer country exploits the poorer one, even where the latter gains by the exchange." — Marx, Theories of Surplus Value
